articles.title: Football Daily - Record breaking night as Liverpool, City & PSG win - 5 Live reaction - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Kelly Cates is joined by Stephen Warnock, Ashley Young, Tom Allnutt and Statman Dave.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 20 Oct 2026 , · 27 mins

Kelly Cates is joined by Stephen Warnock, Ashley Young, Tom Allnutt and Statman Dave to react to what was a record breaking night in the Champions League. Andoni Iraola managed to scrape past his former assistant Inigo Perez as Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3. Manchester City made lightwork of AEK Athens without Erling Haaland as Phil Foden stepped up with a hat-trick as they won 5-1. In the tie all eyes were on, Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 in a thriller at the Parc des Princes. articles.title: Uno a uno del Barcelona: Xavi Espart se presenta ante Europa
articles.standfirst: Analizamos el rendimiento de los azulgranas y el planteamiento de Hansi Flick
articles.summary: Analizamos el rendimiento de los azulgranas y el planteamiento de Hansi Flick
articles.body: Aunque el Barcelona perdió en el Parque de los Príncipes, sí hubo un azulgrana que se presentó en Europa. Xavi Espart disputó su primer encuentro de Champions y lo hizo a lo grande: en un escenario de lujo y jugando de lateral derecho. El canterano estuvo muy sólido en defensa e, incluso, marcó el primero de la noche del Barça. Eso sí, pese al marcador, el mejor de la noche fue Joan García. Primera parte: Los azulgranas sumaron un nuevo partido sin dejar la portería a cero en Champions. El examen en París, eso sí, era más que exigente. El PSG chutó en varias ocasiones en los primeros compases, pero sin mayores problemas, hasta que en el minuto 25 el catalán se lució a disparo de Ferran Torres. Detuvo el balón con la cara. ¡Qué partido del meta de Sallent! Estuvo excelente en una triple ocasión de los franceses antes de la media hora. Hasta seis paradas firmó el catalán antes del minuto 30. No pudo hacer nada, eso sí, en el gol de Doué. Nota al descanso: 8 Segunda parte: Salió también muy entonado en el segundo tiempo con una buena parada ante Hakimi en el uno a uno. No pudo hacer absolutamente nada en los goles del PSG. Pese a los cuatro tantos encajados, fue un buen partido del catalán. Nota al final: 8,5 Primera parte: descansó contra el Betis. En el Parque de los Príncipes regresó al once y se mantuvo en el lateral izquierdo. Vio la amarilla muy pronto, en el minuto 17. El PSG llegaba mucho a las inmediaciones del área del Barcelona. Doué le dio muchos problemas. Nota al descanso: 5,5 Segunda parte: Se situó a la derecha en el minuto 74 tras cambiar Hansi Flick a Xavi Espart y dar entrada a Balde. No estuvo bien en el cuarto tanto del PSG, el de Fabián. Nota al final: 5,5 Primera parte: Sin duda, la defensa afrontaba un examen más que exigente y Cubarsí fue una de las piezas básicas de la retaguardia. Tuvo muchísimo trabajo el de Estanyol, pero muy correcto. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Estuvo muy exigido. No tuvo errores graves. Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: Gerard Martín no pudo acabar el partido contra el Betis por un pisotón en el talón. Pese a ello, salió de inicio junto a Cubarsí. La defensa se multiplicó para frenar el poderío ofensivo del PSG. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: No estuvo bien en el cuarto tanto del PSG. En la recta final competió algunas imprecisiones. Nota al final: 5,5 Primera parte: El canterano es la gran sensación de este inicio de temporada y salió de inicio en el partido de mayor exigencia hasta el momento... y cumplió con creces. Se situó en el lateral derecho por las lesiones de Koundé y Eric García. Se multiplicó en defensa y buscó ayudar en tareas ofensivas. No pesó el escenario. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Muy concentrado los 74 minutos que estuvo sobre el verde. El partido que estaba firmando el canterano se vio recompensado con el gol del 1-1 a pase de Fermín. Se creció aún más tras el tanto. En el 57' robó un balón a Kvaratskhelia, pero Raphinha no pudo culminar la jugada. Dejó el césped en el 74'. Nota al final: 8 Primera parte: El canario cometió un par de imprecisiones en los primeros compases impropias de él. Eso sí, se intentó quitar el mal sabor de boca con una jugada individual, que terminó en córner. A partir de ese momento, fue en línea ascendente y se convirtió en una pieza clave. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Hansi Flick le sentó en el minuto 60 buscando dosificar las cargas del canario, que se sacrificó. Nota al final: 7 Primera parte: Marc Bernal fue la gran sorpresa de la noche. El catalán formó junto a Pedri y descansó Rodri. No estuvo demasiado bien el mediocentro. No terminó de dejarse ver. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: El canterano no tuvo casi contacto con el balón. Dejó el terreno de juego en el 60'. Nota al final: 5 Primera parte: Tras firmar una excelente segunda parte contra el Galatasaray y un cruce completísimo en La Cartuja, Lamine Yamal no estuvo bien en el primer tiempo en el Parque de los Príncipes. Estaba muy vigilado y, cada vez que recibía, aunque no fuese en zona de peligro, le saltaban varios jugadores del PSG a la presión. Cometió varios errores en algunos pases y el más grave fue el que dio pie a la jugada del gol de Doué. Nota al descanso: 5,5 Segunda parte: Salió con una marcha más y se fue creciendo conforme pasan los minutos. En el 64' lanzó un caño espectacular a Lucas. Y apareció en el 79'. Menudo golazo de Lamine Yamal que, tras jugada individual y sin tener ángulo, pone el balón al fondo de la red por el primer palo. Nota al final: 8 Primera parte: Dani Olmo descansó contra el Betis. Tuvo en el minuto 14 la ocasión más clara tras una bonita transición entre Gordon y Raphina, que fue fuera. Tuvo que dejar el terreno de juego en el minuto 27 con molestias físicas. ¡Qué lástima! Estaba jugando bien el catalán. Nota al descanso: 7 Primera parte: También descansó el sábado. El inglés tuvo una buena ocasión en el minuto 10, pero no llegó a rematar. No estuvo tan descarado como en otros compromisos. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Al inglés le gana el salto Lucas Hernández. Un poco apagado en el segundo tiempo. Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: El capitán ya está de vuelta. El azulgrana estaba encontrando portería gracias a su velocidad, pero no mandó encontró el camino del gol. Tuvo dos ocasiones claras antes del minuto 20. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Dejó el terreno de juego en el minuto 60. Nota al final: 6 Saltó al césped en el minuto 27 por la lesión de Olmo. Tuvo una clarísima en el minuto 40' con un mano a mano con el portero. Posiblemente, la más clara de los azulgranas en el primer tiempo. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Dio la asistencia del gol a Xavi Espart. Nota al final: 6 Entró en el campo en el minuto 60. El partido se volvió loco. Nota al final: 5 Saltó al campo en el 60'. Flick buscó poner una marcha más con el andaluz, pero no terminó teniendo el impacto buscado. Nota al final: 5 Salió en el 60'. Aportó más en defensa que en ataque. Nota al final: 5 Salió en el 74'. Testimonial. Nota al final: 5 Primera parte: El técnico ha tenido que buscar soluciones a las muchas bajas en defensa. De hecho, solo tiene cuatro zagueros del primer equipo disponibles, y todos están en el once. Se le vio enfadado durante algunos compases del primer tiempo por las imprecisiones de su equipo. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Movió el banquillo buscando dosificar a sus jugadores. Nota al final: 5,5

articles.title: Van Bronckhorst: "No es el césped que se espera en la Champions"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Feyenoord, crítico en la previa con el estado del campo de La Cartuja
articles.summary: El técnico del Feyenoord, crítico en la previa con el estado del campo de La Cartuja
articles.body: El entrenador del Feyenoord, Giovanni van Bronckhorst, lamentó esta tarde en rueda de prensa el estado del césped del estadio La Cartuja, donde se medirán este miércoles (21.00 horas) con el Betis en la tercera jornada de la liguilla de la Champions League, porque "no está en óptimas condiciones", pero no buscó excusas y dijo que su equipo saldrá "a ganar". Van Bronckhorst defiende que "no es el tipo de césped que se espera en la Champions", tras haber "jugado en un terreno de juego óptimo en los últimos partidos, pero éste no lo está tanto", dijo, aunque admitió que será una circunstancia que "penalizará a ambos equipos". El técnico neerlandés de origen indonesio, que se enfrentará al PSV en la próxima jornada de la Eredivisie, en la que el Feyenoord es líder invicto, aseguró que "ahora mismo no se debe pensar" en el conjunto de Eindhoven, ya que está en Sevilla "para ganar y sumar los tres puntos", algo que "es posible, porque todos los jugadores están disponibles y en forma". Van Bronckhorst respondió con un rotundo "sí" a la pregunta de si una victoria del Feyenoord sobre el Betis podría considerarse una sorpresa, pues recalcó sobre el conjunto español que se ha "fijado en cómo han jugado en los últimos partidos". Así, subrayó que los béticos "le ganaron al Oporto (3-2) y, en el partido (de LaLiga) contra el Barcelona, perdieron (2-5), pero jugaron muy bien; en definitiva, el Barcelona gana por la calidad que posee, pero el Betis demuestra cada semana que es muy bueno", aseveró. El que fuera lateral zurdo internacional neerlandés opinó finalmente que "como ex jugador del Barcelona" espera que "Lamine Yamal gane el Balón de Oro", ya que es "el mejor jugador del mundo" que juega en el que "ahora mismo es el mejor equipo del mundo, el Barcelona", si bien puntualizó que "el PSG está cerca". Nacho Ferri acompañó al entrenador del Feyenoord en rueda de prensa: "Volver a España siempre es especial, como lo fue cuando fuimos a Barcelona, sobre todo por la familia". El delantero habló del proyecto de Frankfurt cuando tuvo otras opciones de pequeño al elegir al cuadro alemán con solo 16 años: "La oferta aquella era buena, también había otra cultura. Considero que fue un paso importante para mi carrera y que acerté". Para el valenciano "es importante rendir en todos los partidos, tanto en casa como fuera" y aseguró que "significa mucho jugar fuera en esta competición para tratar de conseguir los puntos, trataremos de lograrlo mañana".

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "El PSG demostró que es mejor que nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El preparador valora el encuentro de Champions disputado en París
articles.summary: El preparador valora el encuentro de Champions disputado en París
articles.body: Hansi Flick valoró este martes el encuentro contra el PSG, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la Champions League. El Barça cayó 4-2 en París y vio frenada en seco su histórica racha: enlazaba 11 triunfos. Partido "Ha sido un partido fantástico, de los dos equipos. El PSG ha demostrado que es un equipo mejor que nosotros. Hemos perdido, pero hemos aprendido. Los errores suceden. Pero lo hecho en las últimas semanas es fantástico. Hoy no era fácil, los jugadores han corrido mucho y han intentado jugar. Lo que pasó tras Sevilla, con la recuperación, no fue la mejor. No es una excusa. Tenemos que aprender. Estamos en octubre y en octubre no se ganan títulos, la Champions se gana en junio". Segunda parte "Ellos tienen mucha calidad, en la transición... hemos intentado defender. Pero en los últimos 15 minutos no estuvimos frescos. No es una excusa. Hay que ver qué pasó tras Sevilla, no hicimos la mejor preparación. Hay que analizarlo y hacer las cosas mejor en el futuro". Dani Olmo "Veremos qué tiene. Ha tenido un golpe y siente dolor. Está muy decepcionado. No sabemos el alcance de la lesión. Ya veremos". Xavi Espart "Ha jugado un partido fantástico. Ha marcado el gol. Es increíble el nivel al que juega. Se entrenó la temporada pasada, y se vio su nivel. Hizo la pretemporada y mostró un nivel espectacular. Tiene calidad, y lo ha demostrado contra el PSG. Ha marcado. Hace un gran trabajo". Clásico "Tenemos que hacer cambios. Eric y Jules están lesionados. Los laterales han jugado un buen partido. Hay que ver las cosas positivas, porque las hay". Defensa "Creo que contra el City, el PSG también hizo muchos goles. Al final, los últimos 10 minutos, el equipo bajó, y encajamos el cuarto. Pero he visto cosas muy buenas. Tenemos potencial. No soy negativo. Ha sido una buena experiencia. Tenemos que hacerlo mejor". Lecciones "Creo que Joan ha estado fantástico. Hemos tenido ocasiones, que tenemos que materializar. Hay que jugar con más calma. Hay que vigilar las distancias entre los jugadores. Lo tenemos que hacer mejor". Rodri "Sí, descansó porque hay partido contra el Real Madrid. Jugó con la selección, y después con nosotros. Jugamos muy bien en la primera mitad. Bernal estuvo fantástico. Fue una buena solución. Rodri estará fresco para el domingo".

articles.title: Ratings: Alvarez scores at last as 10-man Atlético draw at Stuttgart
articles.summary: Ten-man Atlético Madrid hung on by the skin of their red-and-white teeth to draw 1-1 away to VfB Stuttgart in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night. The...
articles.body:
Ten-man Atlético Madrid hung on by the skin of their red-and-white teeth to draw 1-1 away to VfB Stuttgart in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night.

The German side came flying out of the blocks, blowing Atleti away with a dominant first-half display. They preyed on the fact that Diego Simeone's side tends to struggle with intensity, and from a rojiblanco point of view, the absence of Cuti Romero exacerbated this. Jamie Leweling opened the scoring after 35 minutes, and it had long been coming.

Things looked to be improving in the second half; Ademola Lookman set up Julián Alvarez's first goal of the season within two minutes of the restart, but a costly Morten Hjulmand red card turned the game back in Stuttgart's favour.

Given the circumstances, it did feel like a point gained rather than two dropped, as Atleti sit with four points from a possible nine after three games of the league phase played.

Here are Into the Calderón's player ratings for this one.

Jan Oblak: On his 550th game for the club, Goatblak was the man of the match, for me. He was forced into action early on with an unreal save before even 30 seconds had elapsed, and another as the clock hit 10 minutes. A commanding display as Stuttgart bombarded his penalty area with their man advantage, but Oblak wasn't letting anything get past him in the second half. He has reason to say that his teammates let him down tonight. 8

Marcos Llorente: The three free-flowing, high-intensity Stuttgart attacking midfielders behind the striker caused Llorente a lot of issues, with the evidence coming right from the off. He was caught on the ball under severe pressure inside the first minute which led to Oblak having to make a miracle save. Ended up playing as a right-sided center back once the team was down to ten men, and then in midfield for the last portion of the match. 6

Marc Pubill: The Into the Calderón WhatsApp group spent much of the match speculating whether Pubill's recent heightened sense of fame has had an effect on his focus during games, or whether his new contract has afforded him a feeling of complacency. Either way, spending 90% of his post-World Cup summer drunk hasn't done much good for his fitness. I thought he was miles off the pace tonight, looking slow and tired-looking throughout. 4

Dávid Hancko: Probably Atleti's most consistent threat due to his ability to get on the end of set pieces with headers that weren't too far off. Showed his long-range passing qualities which are always a delight, and held firm toward the end to stop Stuttgart finding a second. 7

Alejandro Grimaldo: On a night when few shone, I thought Grimaldo didn't do much wrong on the whole. Couldn't get anything going offensively, but was able to hold his ground with defensive duties, that no colchonero will have any complaints about. He'll have to show more of these sorts of performances if Simeone is to trust him fully at left-back. 6

Giuliano Simeone: I'm unsure if this was his match to start, but it definitely came to be a game he was required in once Atleti went a man down. Was ultimately brought off towards the end for more of a target man figure up top. Not one of his best performances. 4

Pablo Barrios: Pablito had his match-running ability put to the test (and essentially shown up) tonight, not afforded a second of time on the ball by the opposition. Had a chance to put Atleti a goal up but the angle proved too tight. Time to keep getting the boy fitter so he can withstand these tough away nights in Europe. 5

Morten Hjulmand: The Dane made a crucial error getting sent off just at the moment of the match when Atleti looked to be getting themselves back on top. The tackle was reckless and needless, showing signs of his clumsy tendencies which seem to crop up now and then. 3

Álex Baena: A tough night after taking up a starring role at the weekend. Álex didn't have much luck on the left side of the pitch in the first half. Just when he was looking to have an influence on the match from a number 10 role behind the striker, he was sacrificed for Johnny Cardoso, who had to come on when Hjulmand was sent off. 5

Julián Alvarez: A first half which had me begging for him to be taken off at the break was completely overturned inside the first two minutes of the restart when he finally scored his first goal of the season. He gave the ball away in the build up for the game's opening goal and was generally so loose, but his first-time left-footed finish from Lookman's low cross reminded us all of the quality that still lives on inside la araña . 6

Jonathan David: Much of a spare part in the first half; Atleti would have been better off starting with another midfielder given the way Stuttgart came flying out of the blocks. The instant impact of the man who replaced him justified his half-time hooking. Not necessarily his fault, just wasn't his game to start. 4

Ademola Lookman: The birthday boy had an instant impact of the bench, with an assist just 90 seconds into his second-half appearance. There wasn't too much to shout about from then on, but was forced into a brief stint as a lone striker, before being pulled out wide again. He must be frustrated with the constant changing of positions mid-match. Another goal contribution to keep the momentum building back up. 6

Johnny Cardoso: He looked like a man recovering from a stomach bug, but was able to steady the ship just enough to keep the score level at full time. I don't think he was expecting to play tonight, but can be proud of the minutes that he did. 6

Obed Vargas: He was never going to have an impression on this kind of game with the 12 minutes he was given, but it's nice to know that El Cholo hasn't forgotten Vargas exists. And probably helped remind the fans, too. 4

Robin Le Normand: Did well not to completely cock it up. But in all seriousness, that was all he had to do, and definitely played his part in making sure his team came away with something from this match. 5

Alexander Sørloth: Came on to bully the opposition about a bit for the last few mins, which he executed perfectly. Still working his way back to full fitness, but I do wonder what Sørloth's season looks like from here on in. I'd have thought he'd only become a regular if one of David or Alvarez picks up a lengthy injury. 5

articles.title: Rio Ngumoha shines in comeback Villarreal win but unsung Liverpool hero was true star
articles.summary: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: Andoni Iraola recovered from the worst half-hour of his Anfield tenure so far to earn victory in a seven-goal thriller
articles.body:
It might have been fitting that, on the night the watching Ian Rush 's 65th birthday, the goals flowed at Anfield. Yet even as Liverpool celebrated their most prolific ever No 9, it was more about the man in the No 10 shirt.

The vast majority of Rush's record 346 goals for Liverpool were penalty-box finishes and if much of Alexis Mac Allister 's best work comes in rather deeper positions, the midfielder displayed his predatory streak. In the process, he ensured that Andoni Iraola 's attempts to rest and rotate, which looked likely to backfire after the worst half-hour of his reign , did not cost Liverpool.

If both the teamsheet and the opening stages suggested Iraola was either being generous to his old teammate and assistant Inigo Perez or had underestimated his former sidekick, by the final whistle Liverpool were second in the embryonic Champions League table.

And if they scarcely resembled potential continental champions, Iraola's taste of European nights at Anfield has brought twin continental comebacks, each featuring a starring role from Mac Allister. It was witnessed by his near namesake, Gary McAllister , himself no stranger to important goals in Europe for Liverpool.

It was the kind of talismanic display that Dominik Szoboszlai provided last season. But with the Hungarian injured and Iraola benching the three biggest signings in Liverpool's history, they needed someone to supply the inspiration. Mac Allister obliged.

He was aided by the excellent Rio Ngumoha while Ronald Araujo's equaliser again underlined what a fine bit of business Liverpool did by borrowing the Uruguayan from Barcelona . Florian Wirtz , one of the £364m trio held in reserve, came off the bench to score the fourth.

But Mac Allister, scorer of a winner against Atletico Madrid and, on another occasion when Iraola fielded a weakened team, the opener against Tottenham, was pivotal. His footballing intelligence gives him an eye for goal. A diminutive figure may have been the smallest man in the penalty box but he rose highest to glance in a header from Kostas Tsimikas ' corner. He timed his run into the penalty box perfectly to put Liverpool ahead, crashing in a shot from six yards off the underside of the bar and following a cutback from Ngumoha. It was the 18-year-old's second assist of the night.

The first came when Araujo snuck in at the far post to capitalise on poor defending by Cardona and head in the teenager's cross. It was, albeit indirectly, a second goal from a corner and a second in as many Champions League games for Araujo. 'Big Ron' is proving a big threat from set-pieces.

After Mac Allister doubled his tally for the night, Wirtz drove in Liverpool's fourth following a pass from Cody Gakpo , who was making his first appearance for a month.

He had been summoned at half-time when Ryan Gravenberch , who had begun as the No 10, moved to right-back in place of Araujo. Iraola had left Liverpool's three £100m men on the bench. After half an hour, it seemed he would need to summon them straight away. Instead, he waited before introducing Wirtz. By the time Alexander Isak came on, Liverpool led. They had four goals to their name when Bradley Barcola joined them.

For Liverpool, it was a 16th win in 19 group-stage games since the Champions League expanded, for Villarreal a seventh straight away defeat in Europe. It could, though, have been very different.

Iraola's version of his strongest available side was his freshest, with six changes. A fixture list of Brighton , Chelsea and Arsenal may have been prominent in his thoughts. Yet Liverpool scarcely showed sharpness at the start. They were strangely passive, applying too little pressure to the players on the ball. Their offside trap malfunctioned. They committed individual errors.

The worst came from Virgil van Dijk . An attempt to head the ball back to Alisson was horribly misdirected, the Liverpool captain only finding Georges Mikautadze, who angled a shot past the goalkeeper. Van Dijk had his hands up in apology immediately.

Villarreal's second came when they pierced the offside trap with two runners. Nathan Saliba slid a pass through; Villarreal had two men played onside by Tsimikas and Sergi Cardona slid his shot past Alisson.

Even after seemingly sealing victory, Liverpool afforded them a lifeline. After conceding three goals to LASK last week, they let Villarreal get a third through Tani Oluwaseyi's calm far-post finish; the stand-in right-back Gravenberch gave him too much room.

The danger was that Iraola and Perez, who had shared so much, would share the points. This was a reunion for the former double act, even if it seemed that Iraola had not warned his friend about the weather. Perez did not even don a coat in the Merseyside rain. His attire was more suitable for the Spanish sun but this was a night of Anfield chaos.

articles.title: Hermoso: “We’re a tough team, I like what I’m seeing.”
articles.summary: Following the 4-0 victory against Slovan Bratislava, Roma defender Mario Hermoso, who scored the temporary 1-0 lead, spoke to Sky Sport.“For us, it’s crucial...
articles.body:
Following the 4-0 victory against Slovan Bratislava, Roma defender Mario Hermoso, who scored the temporary 1-0 lead, spoke to Sky Sport.

"For us, it's crucial to follow the coach's instructions, do things well, and win. It's also important to keep a clean sheet."

"Today was a really, really important match. We'd struggled after the defeat here against Real Madrid, and we absolutely needed to win this game, also for the standings."

"Certainly, it's an important aspect, not just for us defenders, but for the entire team. We're a tough team, who want to play with great intensity and always implement what the coach asks of us. That's why keeping a clean sheet is crucial. We also have great talent up front, and we need to try to get as many balls as possible close to the opponent's penalty area to allow our attackers to score."

"We have a strong team, a complete squad, and quality players in every position. We must continue to work and be the team we are. We all strive every day to give our all, and that says a lot about us, about the quality of the squad, and about the work the coach and the sporting director are doing. We must continue on this path, because it's great to see Roma like this."

articles.title: PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 in Champions League thriller to underline European title credentials
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain strengthened their position as Champions League favourites with an entertaining 4-2 victory over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tue...
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain strengthened their position as Champions League favourites with an entertaining 4-2 victory over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday evening.

The reigning European champions extended their unbeaten run in the competition to 13 matches, ending Barcelona's perfect start to the 2026-27 season.

Goals from Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz secured another statement victory for Luis Enrique's side, who maintained their position at the top of the league-phase standings.

PSG began aggressively, pressing Barcelona into mistakes and creating several opportunities inside the opening five minutes.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the post after Pedri surrendered possession, while Doue and Ousmane Dembele forced saves from Joan Garcia.

Barcelona gradually recovered, with Raphinha testing Matvey Safonov following a promising attacking move.

PSG suffered a setback when Dembele sustained an apparent hamstring injury and was replaced by Ferran Torres before half-time.

However, the hosts continued creating opportunities, with Garcia producing several impressive saves to keep Barcelona level.

Their resistance finally ended in the 38th minute when Doue capitalised on another turnover and drove a powerful low shot into the bottom corner.

Fermin Lopez squandered an opportunity to equalise shortly afterwards, allowing PSG to preserve their advantage at the interval.

Barcelona responded strongly after the restart and levelled through 19-year-old Xavi Espart, who marked his Champions League debut with an excellent near-post finish.

Hansi Flick's side subsequently gained control and threatened to complete the turnaround.

Torres struck the woodwork from close range, but PSG immediately punished the visitors emphatically when Hernandez headed home from the resulting corner.

Barcelona refused to surrender, with Lamine Yamal producing a brilliant individual effort to restore parity in the 78th minute.

The teenager escaped Warren Zaire-Emery before squeezing his finish past Safonov from a difficult angle.

However, PSG responded almost immediately through Vitinha, whose superb volley from outside the penalty area restored their lead.

Ruiz then completed the scoring, converting Achraf Hakimi's low delivery to secure an emphatic victory.

The result leaves PSG with nine points from their opening three Champions League fixtures, while Barcelona remain on six.

Luis Enrique's team have now beaten Manchester City and Barcelona in successive European matches, reinforcing their credentials as serious contenders to retain the trophy.

Barcelona, meanwhile, have conceded in 18 consecutive Champions League games, highlighting defensive vulnerabilities that continue to undermine their attacking quality.

PSG will visit Villarreal on November 3, while Barcelona host Aston Villa as they attempt to recover from their first defeat of the campaign.

articles.title: Bristol Rovers 1-2 Salford
articles.summary: Salford strengthened their lead at the League Two summit as first-half goals from Brendan Wiredu and Daniel Udoh secured a hard-fought 2-1 win over Bristol Rovers.
articles.body:
Peter Cklamovski's side battled their way to a sixth successive victory as they withstood a spirited Gas fightback after the break to stretch their lead over second-placed Barnet to four points - albeit having played two games more.

The in-form Ammies, last beaten in the league back in August, took control on six minutes when midfielder Wiredu's whipped shot from 20 yards fled over Brad Young's dive.

They made the most of more flat-footed defending on 20 minutes when Udoh nipped in ahead of his marker to tuck home Luke Molyneux's near-post cross.

Rovers wasted a potential lifeline when Ellis Harrison thumped a 54th-minute penalty against the crossbar after Molyneux upended Clinton Mola.

But Steve Evans' team were not to be denied for long as left-back Jack Sparkes beat Will Norris with a curling 20-yard free-kick.

It set the scene for a tense finale but Salford held firm and condemned their hosts to a fourth straight league defeat.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Gillingham 1-1 Port Vale
articles.summary: Half-time substitute Keyrol Figueroa rescued a point for Port Vale as they came from behind to secure a 1-1 draw against Gillingham at Priestfield.
articles.body:
Figueroa prodded home from close range after the Gills failed to clear a ball into the box, cancelling out Ronan Hale's first-half opener from the penalty spot.

In a quiet first half, the best of the chances fell to Tom Eaves, who headed a Nick Freeman cross wide of the right hand post for the hosts.

Marko Marosi then produced a brilliant save to prevent the Gills from going in front via Andy Smith's header after 35 minutes.

However, he was beaten on 42 minutes when a penalty was awarded for a foul on Ethan Coleman by George Hall, with Hale duly firing home from 12 yards.

Gareth Ainsworth's men should have added a second shortly after the interval, but Eaves was unable to make the most of Hale's deflected shot, before Armani Little fired over.

Vale drew level in the 66th minute when the home defence were unable to clear a ball into their box, and Figueroa was well-placed to find the net.

Kyle Dempsey, another half-time sub, went close to netting the winner for Vale, but his free-kick was well saved by Ollie Wright.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Cheltenham 4-2 Fleetwood
articles.summary: Cheltenham ended a three-game losing run in League Two with a 4-2 home victory over Fleetwood.
articles.body:
The Robins led 3-0 at half-time, going in front after 17 minutes when Charlie McCann's corner was spilled into his own net by Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch.

Cheltenham doubled their lead when Lynch parried well to deny Jake Evans but fellow Leicester loanee Kirsten Otchere followed up for the first goal of his senior career in the 25th minute.

Fleetwood nearly responded less than two minutes later when Rhys Bennett's header hit the bar.

Cheltenham were celebrating again when McCann's incisive pass set up Jake Evans for his fourth goal of the season in the 39th minute.

Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor sent on three substitutes at half-time and two of them combined to pull one back five minutes into the second half as Ched Evans nodded in Crispin McLean's cross.

Ched Evans converted from the penalty spot to make it 3-2 in the 65th minute after Shaun Rooney was fouled by Jonathan Tomkinson.

But Freddy Willcox touched in McCann's corner in the 80th minute to restore Cheltenham's two-goal advantage.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Real Madrid and Barcelona remain keen on Arsenal star
articles.summary: Martin Zubimendi was expected to play an even bigger role at Arsenal this season after becoming an important member of the team last campaign. However, the m...
articles.body:
Martin Zubimendi was expected to play an even bigger role at Arsenal this season after becoming an important member of the team last campaign. However, the midfielder has struggled to secure regular playing time since the new campaign began, raising questions about his future at the Emirates.

The Spaniard has also been played out of position when given opportunities, making his situation different from what many expected. Mikel Arteta was keen on working with him, but Zubimendi could now consider his options if his role does not improve.

Real Madrid and Barcelona monitor Zubimendi

Zubimendi attracted interest from Real Madrid and Chelsea during the last transfer window, although neither club completed a move for him. Speculation about a possible return to Spain has continued , with fresh interest emerging from two of the country's biggest clubs.

According to Team Talk , Real Madrid are still monitoring the midfielder, while Barcelona have also entered the race to sign him. The Catalan club reportedly believe he could strengthen their squad and sees an opportunity to recruit him if Arsenal cannot offer him the regular football he wants.

Barcelona could look to take advantage of Zubimendi's current situation, particularly if his lack of minutes continues over the coming months. A move could potentially happen in January or at the end of the season, depending on how circumstances develop at Arsenal.

Martin Zubimendi (Photo by Yong Teck Lim/Getty Images)

Zubimendi's situation presents an important question for Arsena l. The club brought him in with expectations that he would contribute significantly, but his limited involvement so far could encourage interest from teams prepared to offer him a more prominent role.

Arteta will have to consider whether the midfielder can become a more regular part of his plans as the campaign progresses. Arsenal may prefer to keep him and give him more opportunities, rather than allow a player with his qualities to leave before he has fully settled into the team.

However, if the situation remains unchanged, interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona could become increasingly difficult to ignore. Both clubs may view the midfielder as an opportunity to strengthen their squads, particularly if he becomes available.

articles.title: York 1-1 Accrington
articles.summary: Ollie Pearce's 90th-minute header rescued a 1-1 draw for York at home to Accrington.
articles.body:
It had looked like Josh Woods' sixth goal of the season would earn Stanley a first win on the road since February, but Pearce also extended his own tally to six with the late leveller.

Woods opened the scoring in the 62nd minute when, having won a free-kick close to the left touchline, he then glanced a header inside the far post from Stefan Mols' teasing delivery.

The visitors wasted excellent chances to extend their lead through Woods and substitute Connor Grant, while David Tutonda was denied by a fine save by Alfie McNally.

Instead, it was Pearce who stuck, heading in from six yards after Harry Boyes had crossed from the right.

The result was cruel on John Doolan's men, who will still take solace from extending their beaten run in all competitions to eight games.

articles.title: Barnet 1-3 Swindon
articles.summary: Aaron Drinan's brace helped Swindon to a 3-1 victory at Barnet, handing the hosts their first league defeat of the season.
articles.body:
Barnet threatened inside seven minutes when Kabongo Tshimanga's cross deflected into Stephan Negru's path, but his effort was saved by Swindon goalkeeper Connor Ripley.

The visitors responded against the run of play as Mitch Clark surged forward on a swift counter-attack before curling into the bottom corner for his first goal for the club.

Barnet continued to press, with Charlie Lakin volleying narrowly wide before Ripley was called into action to produce five saves in quick succession.

Swindon doubled their advantage when Matty Virtue's superb low cross found captain Drinan, who poked home past Matthew Cox.

Drinan struck again just two minutes later, capitalising on a lapse in concentration from Barnet's defence before rifling his effort into the net.

Swindon started the second half brightly as Joe Snowdon drilled an effort straight at Cox, before Barnet pulled a goal back late on through Tshimanga, who converted from close range.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Exeter 2-0 Crewe
articles.summary: Crewe's unbeaten start to the League Two season was ended as Exeter ran out 2-0 winners at St James Park.
articles.body:
Alex had won five and drawn six of their first 11 games this season, but Anthony Scully's first-half penalty and a late Reece Cole strike settled an even contest to lift Exeter into the top half of the table for the first time this term.

Exeter dominated the first half with Charlie Cummins stinging the palms of Tom Booth and George Birch causing problems. It was the young Academy graduate who was upended inside the box by Joe White on 21 minutes, which led to Scully converting the resultant penalty.

Cummins was narrowly wide with a curling shot from an acute angle as Exeter continued to dominate, although Jordan Gibson was off target with a shot from 20 yards for Alex.

The second half saw Crewe kick into gear with Gibson and Matus Holicek denied by Jack Bycroft in the Exeter goal. But try as they might, they could not breach an Exeter defence that has conceded just six goals in 12 games this season.

Exeter wrapped it up in stoppage time when Cole won the ball out on the touchline and with so many men forward, he had the freedom of St James Park to run through and smash home a second for the Grecians.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Luis Enrique: "Sería una trampa pensar que somos los mejores"
articles.standfirst: El técnico asturiano elogia el juego de los culés
articles.summary: El técnico asturiano
articles.body: Luis Enrique compareció ante los medios de comunicación para analizar el partido que enfrentó al PSG y el Barcelona. El técnico asturiano aseguró que, pese al resultado, sería una trampa pensar que son los mejores, destacó la buena recuperación tras pérdida que había hecho su equipo en campo contrario y elogió al Barcelona. "He visto un partido como esperaba. Muy difícil y complicado. No te das cuenta del nivel del Barça hasta que te enfrentas a ellos. Ha sido muy igualado. Creo que hemos estado muy buen en la primera parte, controlando muy bien al Barça y recuperando balones en campo contrario. En la segunda parte hemos tenido 10 ó 15 minutos de sufrimiento, pero luego hemos vuelto a retomar, nos hemos adelantado en el marcador y eso nos ha tranquilizado" "Para poder ganar partidos y títulos importantes y contra rivales del mismo nivel que tú, hay que saber adaptarse a las situaciones de juego. Hemos tenido que hacer bloque bajo en 15 minutos pero sabemos hacer transiciones. El año pasado con el Bayern nos tocó defender sí o sí. Los rivales son de alto nivel y te pueden ganar los partidos". "No. Esa sería la primera trampa. Si pensamos que somos los mejores o especiales. Hoy hemos hecho un buen trabajo defensivo. Hemos sido superiores en recuperación de balón en campo contrario en la primera parte y eso es gracias a nuestros delanteros. Para quitar el balón a Lamine, Fermín, Olmo... o tienes ayudas o es imposible de defender". "Soy culé. Soy un profesional y disfruto con las victorias de mi equipo":

articles.title: Grimaldo pide explicaciones por el penalti a Hancko y Mateu Lahoz no tiene dudas: "Es clarísimo"
articles.standfirst: El lateral valenciano se mostró muy enfadado con un posible penalti al eslovaco
articles.summary: El lateral valenciano se mostró muy enfadado con un posible penalti al eslovaco
articles.body: Grimaldo no se mordió la lengua al acabar el choque en Stuttgart. El lateral valenciano se mostró sorprendido al comprobar que el VAR no entró a revisar un posible penalti sobre Hancko en un saque de esquina. "Ha habido un penalti clarísimo que no entiendo que el VAR entre en algunas situaciones, no entre en otras. Es algo que no termino de entender, pero creo que en la tele todo el mundo lo ha podido ver", aseguró en zona mixta. "Es una jugada que tenemos para él al primer palo y le chafan ahí. Es un penalti clarísimo. Hace poco nos pitaron a nosotros un penalti en una falta lateral, ahora no lo pitan. Supongo que tendrán que salir a dar alguna explicación", explicó enfadado cuando atendió a los periodistas españoles desplazados a Stuttgart. Una acción que el propio Grimaldo vio en primera persona al ser el jugador que lanzó el saque de esquina de la jugada polémica. "Yo lo veo, yo soy el que saca el córner. Le pisan y va al suelo. Yo creo que ni lo han parado a mirar. No entendemos que no lo miren. Necesitamos que den explicaciones. Saber el motivo por el que unas veces entran y otras no" El excolegiado Mateu Lahoz analizó la jugada polémica de Hancko en Movistar. Para él, la acción era una clara pena máxima. "Es un penalti muy claro y amarilla por temeridad. Si al árbitro se le escapa, que es normal, el VAR tiene imágenes y le debe invitar a ir al monitor", dijo.

articles.title: El PSG fulmina la histórica racha del Barça
articles.standfirst: El conjunto de Luis Enrique evidencia los problemas defensivos de los culés
articles.summary: El conjunto de Luis Enrique evidencia los problemas defensivos de los culés
articles.body: Frenazo en seco. El PSG fulminó esta noche, en el partido disputado en París, la histórica racha de victorias del Barcelona. El conjunto culé llegó al cruce, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la fase de la liguilla de la Champions League, habiendo ganado los once encuentros que había disputado: nueve de LaLiga y dos del torneo continental. Los de Luis Enrique acabaron con su camino triunfal, evidenciando sus problemas defensivos, con un doloroso 4-2. El Barça estuvo irreconocible en Parc des Prince. El bloque catalán encajó una importante goleada: una de las más importantes de los últimos cursos. El PSG sonrojó a los culés endosándole un doloroso, e inesperado, 4-2. Doué, Lucas, Vitinha y Fabián fueron los realizadores del conjunto galo. Los catalanes confirmaron, un cruce más, sus serios problemas defensivos, que se evidencian especialmente en la Champions League. Los azulgranas ya encadenan ¡18! encuentros encajando goles en la máxima competición continental. Este curso, pese a vencer con autoridad en los dos anteriores compromisos europeos, tanto Feyenoord y Galatasaray vieron puerta. Marcaron una diana cada uno. Pero pese a la goleada encajada esta noche en París, Joan García fue el futbolista culé más destacado. Sin el portero catalán, el marcador hubiera sido todavía más abultado. El meta internacional tuvo intervenciones decisivas en las dos partes, con excelentes paradas a Ferran Torres, Hakimi, Kvaratskhelia... La primera derrota del Barcelona de la temporada, tras once encuentros ganados en su mayoría por goleadas, llega justo en una semana importante: el Barça recibe el domingo, en el Spotify Camp Nou, la visita del Real Madrid. Los culés confían en que este revés no les afecte anímicamente y puedan levantarse para el importante cruce de LaLiga. "No nos afectará", sentenció Raphinha.

articles.title: Oblak: "Mejor un punto que nada, pero hemos buscado los tres puntos"
articles.standfirst: El capitán del Atlético se mostró contrariado por el resultado en Stuttgart
articles.summary: El capitán del Atlético se mostró contrariado por el resultado en Stuttgart
articles.body: Jan Oblak fue uno de los más destacados del Atlético en su visita a Stuttgart. El capitán rojiblanco analizó el choque en los micrófonos de Movistar a la conclusión del partido. Análisis del choque: "El partido ha sido el que esperábamos, con una buena presión de ellos en los primeros minutos, en los que no pudimos salir y ellos tuvieron alguna oportunidad. A partir de su gol, jugamos mejor. Empezamos bien la segunda parte, pero con uno menos se complica y es muy difícil en inferioridad ante un equipo que corre y presiona como ellos. Siempre es mejor un punto que ninguno". Reacción: "La segunda parte la hemos empezado bien, hemos venido a ganar, pero con uno menos se ha complicado un poco más. Es normal. Hay que seguir, la Champions es difícil, es difícil ganar a cualquier equipo, pero necesitamos puntos y estar ahí arriba para meternos en la siguiente ronda". La expulsión de Hjulmand: "Lo he visto desde lejos, pero nadie ha protestado, así que parece que sí ha sido. Hay que tener cuidado, pero son cosas que pasan. Cuando vas al suelo, puede pasar eso, que te saquen la roja porque otro llega antes. Pero Hjulmand está jugando muy bien y contra el Espanyol lo hizo fenomenal".

articles.title: Julián Alvarez, un gol para la ‘resurrección’
articles.standfirst: La Araña recupera su 'veneno' con el Atlético 174 días después de marcar al Arsenal el 29 de abril
articles.summary: La Araña recupera su 'veneno' con el Atlético 174 días después de marcar al Arsenal el 29 de abril
articles.body: Cierto es que en el pasado Mundial llegó a marcar (un único gol que se antojó escaso para un delantero de su nivel) y que también aprovecharía el último parón para marcar en uno de los amistosos con Argentina, pero por fin Julián Alvarez ha vuelto a celebrar una diana como rojiblanco. La necesitaba como el comer, tanto por el culebrón protagonizado durante el verano como por la necesidad de recuperar una sensación que no experimentaba como rojiblanco desde el lejanísimo 29 de abril, cuando marcó al Arsenal en el partido de ida de las semifinales de la Champions anterior. Casi seis meses, 174 días para ser más exactos, se le ha resistido a Julián un tanto que, más allá de suponer el número 50 desde que luce la camiseta del Atlético (25 en LaLiga, siete en la Copa y 18 ya en la Champions), se presume como el primero en su resurrección. Ya venía dando señales de su camino hacia la normalidad en los últimos partidos (sin ir más lejos frente al Espanyol ejercería de asistente de Baena), pero no cabe duda de que le faltaba ese gol que le ayudara a desquitarse de todo lo sucedido. De ahí que, aunque su zurdazo a la escuadra no sirviera para ganar, al menos sí valió para anunciar que la Araña vuelve a recuperar su veneno y, sobre todo, que ya no deberá cargar con esa losa tan pesada que le impedía enderezar su nuevo horizonte en el Atlético. Un principio en su redención que no es ajena al vestuario. "También por el partido que hizo, el trabajo en la izquierda. Hizo un golazo, me pone muy contento por él. Le necesitamos para llegar a los lugares que queremos llegar", señalaría Simeone. "Lleva unos partidos creando muchas ocasiones. Es nuestro mejor jugador, es muy importante. Necesitaba este gol y espero que sea el primero de muchos", secundaría Grimaldo.

articles.title: Iñigo Pérez: “La fase clave, que era justo antes del descanso, no la hemos sabido jugar”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Villarreal se muestra autocrítico, a pesar de la buena imagen de su equipo en la derrota ente el Liverpool
articles.summary: El técnico del Villarreal se muestra autocrítico, a pesar de la buena imagen de su equipo en la derrota ente el Liverpool
articles.body: Las palabras de Iñigo Pérez tras la derrota del Villarreal en Anfield reflejaron más autocrítica que consuelo. Pese a reconocer el mérito de haber competido de tú a tú con el Liverpool y haber marcado tres goles en uno de los escenarios más exigentes de Europa, el técnico rechazó refugiarse en las lecturas positivas y puso el foco en los errores que acabaron decidiendo el encuentro (4-3). El entrenador amarillo destacó que su equipo fue capaz por momentos de controlar el partido, generar ocasiones y poner en dificultades a un rival de máximo nivel en un ambiente tan exigente como el de Anfield. Sin embargo, consideró que esos aspectos quedan en un segundo plano después de encajar una derrota. Pérez apuntó especialmente a la gestión emocional de determinados momentos del choque, en particular la fase previa al descanso, donde entendió que su equipo no supo frenar la inercia favorable al Liverpool ni competir con la madurez necesaria para sostener el marcador. ¿Qué aspectos positivos destaca del equipo pese a la derrota? "Cuando pierdes, creo que la lectura positiva queda para unos días más tarde. Ahora mismo, creo que haber marcado tres goles en Anfield y tener por momentos un partido controlado, jugando bien, generando ocasiones ante un tremendo equipo en esta atmósfera, creo que es la parte positiva, visible y sentida por todos los que estábamos en el campo. Pero si tú haces todo eso, marcas tres goles y acabas perdiendo, creo que nuestro deber es atender esa parte". ¿Qué ha fallado? ¿Ha sido algo emocional o también táctico? "Seguro que el entrenador ha hecho cosas mal, no existe el partido perfecto y me tocará hacer autocrítica. Creo que también ha sido visible la parte en la que no hemos podido estar a la altura de un partido como este. Detalles muy simples de no generar inercia emocional, que sabemos que en este estadio se provoca de manera instantánea ante cualquier acción favorable hacia ellos. No lo hemos podido manejar, hemos empatado y después, en el descanso, intentas preparar para lo que viene. Ellos tienen mucho nivel, juegan muy bien, es un gran equipo. Al final hemos podido permanecer dentro del partido, pero creo que la fase clave, que era justo antes del descanso, no la hemos sabido jugar y luego ya es difícil". El equipo está compitiendo bien ante grandes de Europa pese a las derrotas en Dortmund y Liverpool. ¿Le sirve esa lectura positiva? "A mí no me sacian estas lecturas, sé que puede ser una lectura y es una realidad, pero a mí no me genera ni un ápice de tranquilidad. En ambos partidos, tanto en Dortmund como hoy, debemos y podemos ganarlos. El foco debe estar en por qué no los hemos ganado, a pesar de que hay otras lecturas positivas que son ciertas. Pero creo que llevarnos a ese camino nos llevaría a equivocarnos y prefiero ser crítico, ir a corregir e intentar ser perfecto"

articles.title: Lucas Hernández, la última pesadilla para Lamine: "No le he dado espacios y ha funcionado"
articles.standfirst: El lateral fue la apuesta de Luis Enrique para frenar al azulgrana, que marcó un golazo justo cuando el lateral se fue al banquillo
articles.summary: El lateral fue la apuesta de Luis Enrique para frenar al azulgrana, que marcó un golazo justo cuando el lateral se fue al banquillo
articles.body: Lucas Hernández fue uno de los protagonistas del gran duelo entre el PSG y el Barça. Sin Nuno Mendes, Luis Enrique apostó por la experiencia del francés pese a que no tiene muchos minutos. Su último partido de titular en Champions fue en enero de 2025. Lucas celebraba la victoria y hablaba del marcaje a Lamine, al margen de que hizo un golazo de cabeza para volver a adelantar a su equipo (2-1). "Siempre intento darlo todo en el campo, fui agresivo y sin darle mucho espacio y al final ha funcionado", comentó el defensa. "En la charla previa al partido me enteré de que iba a ser titular. Como siempre he hecho, lo di todo en el campo. Es cierto que hay noches mejores que otras, pero esas ganas de darlo todo en el campo nunca me han abandonado y hoy ha dado sus frutos", añadió el jugador. "No estoy acostumbrado a marcar muchos goles, pero al fin y al cabo es un partido de la fase de grupos. Esta noche hemos demostrado que somos un equipo muy bueno. Tendremos que seguir así. A veces hay días en los que te sientes mejor, pero siempre lo he dado todo en el campo y voy a seguir haciéndolo en París", sostiene Lucas. "Me alegro mucho por él, es un jugador que da buen ambiente al grupo y que ha estado hoy excelente. Ha hecho un marcaje increíble a Lamine y además ha marcado un gol. Se lo merece", apuntó Luis Enrique.

articles.title: Man City 5-1 AEK Athens: Phil Foden 'going in right direction' after five star showing
articles.summary: Phil Foden's magnificent man-of-the-match display in Manchester City's Champions League win against AEK Athens serves as a reminder of his talent and ability to influence games.
articles.body:
Phil Foden's magnificent man-of-the-match display in the Champions League against AEK Athens served as a reminder of the prodigious talent that the player still possesses.

After two disappointing seasons in which, by his own admission, he failed to hit the heights expected, there may be those who had forgotten what he can produce.

Being left out of the England squad for the World Cup last summer did not help, but he came into this season telling reporters he was looking forward to a "fresh start" under new manager Enzo Maresca.

Up until last weekend, that fresh start had been a slow burner with the low point of being sent off in the derby against Manchester United in September, before he sparked into life by netting against Ipswich on Saturday.

That was his first Premier League goal in 10 months and a strike that seems to have opened the floodgates, with the 26-year-old netting a superb hat-trick in the 5-1 hammering of Athens at Etihad Stadium on Tuesday.

"I enjoyed that a lot," Foden told TNT Sports. "The lads were great again. We showed determination again. I am a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It is good for my confidence."

Asked if he was returning to his best form, Foden said: "Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps.

"I want to keep working hard and keep being the best I can for the manager and the team."

Foden stars with hat-trick as Man City thrash AEK Athens

A smiling Foden gliding across the turf in full flow is a joy for City fans to watch and he sent them home happy after a performance in which he had a hand in four of the five goals.

Boss Maresca took a risk by making eight changes from the side that beat Ipswich in their last outing, with Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias and Foden the players retained.

Striker Erling Haaland was named in the squad but ultimately given the night off after sustaining a blow to the foot in the previous game, giving Maresca the chance to explore his suggestion that Foden could offer a "solution" in the false nine role.

After starting on the right, he moved into that position later in the game and it paid dividends, with Foden saying he "really enjoyed" the role.

Though there was a brief scare for City at the start of the second half when the visitors pulled a goal back to trail 2-1, they found another gear and were out of sight by the final whistle.

And by then, Foden had become just the third Englishman to score a hat-trick and provide an assist in a Champions League match after Wayne Rooney for Manchester United in 2004 and former team-mate Raheem Sterling for City in 2019.

While the first and third goals were converted from close range, the second was a stunning finish from just inside the area, Foden opening up his body and caressing a first-time effort into the top corner.

"Beautiful - that's the word I would use to describe him," former City defender Joleon Lescott said of Foden on TNT Sports. "His finishing was exquisite.

"I think he has convinced the manager that if Erling Haaland isn't available for any reason throughout the season, then he is the man to play at number nine."

Foden scored 19 goals as City won the Premier League in 2023-24 and was named the Professional Footballers' Association player of the year and the league's player of the season.

He ended last season by failing to score in his last 31 games for club and country but despite the struggles, he signed a new four-year deal in July.

The red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes at Old Trafford could have been damaging but the aim now will be kick on and build on this showing.

"I was very happy with Phil, even before the red card to be honest," said Maresca. "I said since day one that I consider him one of the best English players.

"We know that Phil is a top player. Again, for different reasons, he had some problems in the last two years but he is going to help us.

"That is why we are so keen to have him in the best way."

Former England winger Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "When Phil Foden gets his opportunities tonight, he takes them with both hands. By getting a hat-trick, his confidence is going to be sky high.

"Enzo Maresca is going to be happy he hasn't had to bring on Erling Haaland or Jeremy Doku. He has been able to use the players that are in his squad.

"This is no way a second-string but you have got to go our there and show the manager 'I should be playing'.

"Foden is answering his manager's questions."

articles.body: En mitad de este otoño, Levante y Athletic recuperan un partido que debía haberse jugado la última semana del verano. Ninguno de los dos contendientes ha ganado desde aquella suspensión y el encuentro aprieta a sus respectivos proyectos. Lo de esta noche es para ponerse al día –aunque al Athletic le queda todavía otro suspendido ante el Rayo– y, en base a los puntos, recolocar los objetivos lanzados en tiempos de pretemporada. Empatar ante el Dépor le permite estar fuera de las posiciones de descenso y los puntos en juego le asegurarían plaza en mitad de la tabla. Luís Castro no descarta a Etta Yong, lesionado hace más de un mes y que ya trabaja con normalidad. Por su parte, Hugo Sotelo, que se encuentra en periodo de recuperación de su lesión, y Álex Primo, que regresó este pasado martes a los entrenamientos junto al resto de sus compañeros, serán las ausencias para el partido ante el equipo rojiblanco. Los leones tienen el cuerpo revuelto tras la grave lesión que sufrió Guruzeta el pasado sábado en Mestalla. El delantero, que estará de baja toda la temporada al romperse el cruzado, aparece en el corazón de todos sus compañeros y sería destinatario seguro de la dedicatoria de la victoria. Nico, que ha vuelto a entrenar, no está todavía para cargarse de minutos y en la convocatoria de Terzic vuelve a haber presencia del filial. Olasasgasti vs Gerenabarrena. El centrocampista donostiarra es más que un tododoterreno para el Levante. Es uno de los baluartes en la medular granota y se destaca por su despliegue y facilidad para saltar líneas. En el lado rojiblanco aparece Gerenabarrena, al que Terzic retiró en Mestalla en el descanso y el equipo lo acusó. Gere, que es debutante en el equipo y en la categoría, ha comenzado el curso a un nivel superior al de sus compañeros. El Levante se tiene que hacer fuerte en casa. Cinco encuentros sin ganar son ya demasiados para los granotas. Sin embargo, hoy tendrá enfrente al Athletic, un rival difícil de doblegar. La necesidad de unos chocará con la sobriedad de los otros. La apuesta, unas tablas.

articles.title: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: Rio Ngumoha shines in comeback win
articles.summary: Rio Ngumoha produces a coming-of-age performance in Liverpool's comeback win over Villarreal, writes Aadam Patel.
articles.body:
In a game of seven goals, none were scored by Rio Ngumoha - but this was his night.

The 18-year-old was simply a class apart from the rest in Liverpool's 4-3 win over Villarreal.

It is over a year since Ngumoha burst on to the scene for Liverpool with a memorable stoppage-time winner at Newcastle.

He has been in and out since then, impressing in flashes and even going on to make his England debut earlier this season.

But this performance was different, inspiring his team to a memorable comeback win in the Champions League.

By the time the teenager was replaced in the 74th minute, with Bradley Barcola taking over, the chants of "Rio, Rio, Rio" had repeatedly rung around Anfield.

It was quite the sight to see Alisson embrace Ngumoha shortly after the young man was given Uefa's player of the match award.

"It's up there with one of the best [games] I've played. I enjoyed myself out there and the team helped me a lot," Ngumoha told Amazon Prime.

"Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one versus one, or two versus one, I believe in myself to do it. I'll just keep going and be ruthless."

Liverpool were woeful for much of the first half as they trailed Villarreal by two goals, but Ngumoha took responsibility and began to turn the tide.

After Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back, Ngumoha found space to dink in a delightful ball that was met by Ronald Araujo for an equaliser.

Ater the break, Ngumoha - as he had done all evening - waltzed past Sergi Cardona to set up Mac Allister to give Liverpool the lead.

Florian Wirtz added what proved to be a vital fourth.

Ngumoha inspires Liverpool comeback win - report and player ratings

Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: What Iraola and Ngumoha said

Football Daily: Record breaking night as Liverpool, Man City & PSG win - 5 Live reaction

Contract talks ongoing as Ngumoha's football speaks volumes

The match statistics alone showed what a threat Ngumoha can be.

He had 12 touches in the opposition box, completed seven out of eight dribbles, and registered two crucial assists.

But watching Ngumoha is more than just a numbers experience. There's a fearless nature to his play that can get the crowd going, and he was the one bright spark in a first half where Liverpool lacked any sort of rhythm.

In a game increasingly focused on structures, Ngumoha's raw ability to take a man on is what helps to set him apart.

"He was magnificent tonight," said former Liverpool forward Daniel Sturridge on Amazon Prime.

"On the ball, this kid has so much potential - and I say 'kid', but he's a young man. He has so much quality and it's stuff that you can't teach to be honest.

"What he does with the ball at his feet - that is God-given ability - and his hard work on the training pitch, doing things day in and day out, and being ruthless, is what he said in his interview, and I like that. He wants to be decisive, and I love that."

Ngumoha, who has grown up playing down the left, has struggled to get minutes on his preferred side this season, especially with Cody Gakpo and Barcola often playing down that flank.

But head coach Andoni Iraola wants his wingers to be able to play on both sides and Ngumoha's improvement on the right flank has been impressive in such a short space of time.

Ngumoha also spoke about his rapid development on the right on Saturday, after Liverpool beat Brentford.

"I feel like I've got a lot better playing there from the Newcastle game [at the start of this season] until now," Ngumoha said.

"I'm understanding it more. And going away with England helped a lot as well. I like playing on both sides. It gives me another tool in the toolbox."

Iraola praised Ngumoha's attitude and how he is playing more minutes "endurance-wise" but stressed the need to remember the youngster is not done with his development.

"I am happy with his attitude because he is eager to improve the things we think he needs to improve, and to add more things to his game," Iraola said.

"He has played a lot on the right lately and is feeling so comfortable now, but he is only 18 and still not the full package.

"I hope it continues the same way, but it is not always going to be like this.

"There will be ups and downs in the process, but I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place."

Talks continue over a new deal, with Ngumoha currently on the contract that he signed in September 2025, weeks after his 17th birthday, that tied him down until 2028.

The expectation is that he will sign with more lucrative terms now that he is 18 and - as Ngumoha said at the weekend - those negotiations are going well and in the hands of his agent.

He will focus on letting his football do the talking - as he did on Tuesday night against Villarreal.

What is certain is that Liverpool have a truly special talent on their hands and one that they will hope can entertain the Anfield crowd for years to come.

articles.title: Julian Sayin Injury Update, Latest Updates from OSU's Ryan Day on QB's Timeline, Status for Playoff
articles.summary: Ohio State may be without quarterback Julian Sayin for the rest of the season, including any potential College Football Playoff run.
articles.body:
Ohio State may be without quarterback Julian Sayin for the rest of the season, including any potential College Football Playoff run.

"We're not gonna put any timeline for his injury, but he is out indefinitely," head coach Ryan Day told reporters Tuesday when discussing the injury the quarterback suffered during Saturday's win over Indiana.

Day also revealed the Buckeyes are coming up with a plan in case Sayin does not return for the regular season or postseason while adding it is "doubtful" he will return before the end of the regular season on Nov. 28.

This is a devastating blow to Ohio State's chances at reaching the CFP and competing for a national championship.

Sayin was a Heisman Trophy finalist last season while completing 77 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He led the Buckeyes to an undefeated regular season, although they lost the Big Ten championship game to Indiana and in the CFP to Miami.

He entered the 2026 campaign with NFL draft hype as a presumed Heisman candidate and completed 68.2 percent of his passes for 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions prior to the injury.

The question now is what is next for Ohio State.

Luke Fahey entered Saturday's contest against the Hoosiers but threw incompletions on his two pass attempts and wasn't asked to do much as the visitors relied on their defense to clinch the win.

He is a true freshman and was a 3-star prospect, per 247Sports' composite rankings. By comparison, Tavien St. Clair has been on campus since the 2025 season and was a 5-star recruit in that year's class, per 247Sports' composite rankings.

Fahey may have gotten the call Saturday, but that doesn't mean he will automatically be the long-term starter moving forward now that the situation has changed with Sayin potentially out for the rest of the season.

"Going into the last few games, Luke's been ahead of Tavien in terms of what we've seen, but now that we have a bye week, these guys are both gonna get a lot of reps, and we're gonna start to put together a plan on how we're gonna move forward," Day told reporters . "We're gonna play the guy that gives us the best chance to win."

He continued and said both quarterbacks will get first-team reps.

"We need both guys to practice really well and prepare and understand that we're gonna need them to win a championship," Day said.

It will be anything but easy, as Ohio State still has challenging road games against USC and Nebraska remaining, as well as home games against Oregon, Michigan and Northwestern. It also has a loss to Texas, so there is less room for error than there would be if it was undefeated.

The silver lining for the Buckeyes is whichever quarterback wins the job will still have Jeremiah Smith on the receiving end of passes. But it remains to be seen if that is enough to overcome this significant loss.

articles.title: Champions League sets new goals record this season
articles.summary: It was goals galore again in the Champions League on Tuesday, with the competition setting a new record this season.
articles.body:
More teams, more games - and more goals.

Since the current Champions League format was introduced at the start of the 2024-25 season, Europe's elite club competition has delivered all of the above and more.

Already trending upwards over the past two campaigns, there has been a genuine goals boom in this year's competition.

The 187 goals scored so far have come at an average of 4.16 per game - the highest in Champions League history.

"Look how many goals have been scored, it's phenomenal," ex-Manchester United and England winger Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live. "The attackers are being clinical."

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock described the volume of goals as "incredible" - so how unusual is it?

Not only is the current goals-per-game percentage the highest ever in the Champions League, it is the third highest in European Cup history - behind only 1959-60 (4.19) and 1955-56 (4.38).

While 40 goals were scored across nine games on Tuesday, last week was even more spectacular.

Last Wednesday saw the third highest-scoring day in Champions League history (46 goals), bettered only by the final league-phase matchdays of 2024-25 and 2025-26, when 18 matches took place.

The 78 goals scored across Tuesday and Wednesday last week made matchday two the highest scoring in history.

That was nine more than the total scored on matchday one this season (69) - which, at the time, was the second highest-scoring matchday since the new league phase was introduced in 2024-25.

Will we see the record fall again this week? It's already halfway there.

Doue impresses as PSG beat Barcelona in thriller

Ever since Uefa announced its plans to alter the format of the Champions League in 2021, the impact on matches has been a hot topic. Scrutiny has only increased since the changes were implemented in time for the 2024-25 season.

After beginning life as a six-team invitational tournament in 1955-56 before growing to a 32-team knockout tournament in 1967, the Champions League as we know it began in 1992.

A group stage was added, with the last 16 entering a knockout phase. There was a brief spell with two group stages, but this was reverted back to the single group-stage format for the 2003-04 tournament.

The group stage previously featured 32 teams in eight groups of four, with the top two sides from each of those groups qualifying for the last 16.

For the start of the 2024-25 season, the group stage was replaced with a 36-team league phase, with each side playing eight one-off fixtures instead of six games against three teams.

The top eight finishers qualify directly for the knockout stages, with those placed ninth to 24th entering a two-legged play-off stage.

The bottom eight are eliminated, meaning that after eight matches, 24 sides are still in the competition. Some argue that that creates a lack of jeopardy, which encourages teams to play more expansively.

"I think the entertainment has gone up, although I'm not sure the quality has gone up," The Times football writer Tom Arnott told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"If I'm looking at the games it's brilliant to watch and thrilling because the football itself is fantastic - but what do they mean?

"The lack of jeopardy, why would PSG and Barcelona play for a draw, why not go for it? If you need five wins from the eight games you know you've got some margin there. If you lose it's OK. I think the format allows all the teams to loosen up.

"The entertainment value is there but I think you come away from these matches sometimes and still think 'what does it all mean?'. The lack of jeopardy early on does deliver entertainment."

articles.title: No. 3 Ohio State preparing for Julian Sayin to miss rest of regular season, 'doubtful' he will return after arm injury
articles.summary: Julian Sayin left the Buckeyes' win over Indiana early with an arm injury that will now keep him out indefinitely.
articles.body:
Ryan Day is preparing for a world where Julian Sayin doesn't take the field again at all this season.

The coach for No. 3 Ohio State confirmed Tuesday that his star quarterback is going to be out indefinitely after he went down with a right arm injury in their win over Indiana on Saturday. While he doesn't have a specific timeline for Sayin's return, it's "doubtful" that he will be able to play again in the regular season.

"We're not going to put any timeline on his recovery, but he is out indefinitely. … Based on the nature of the injury, we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season, and then also him not being available for the postseason," Day said, via the Delaware Gazette's Dillon Davis . "Based on that, if he's not able to return this fall, we'll put together a plan for that as well."

Sayin was hit hard from his right side as he went to throw the ball in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes' 19-15 win at Indiana on Saturday. Sayin's throwing arm was pinned awkwardly against his body as he hit the ground, too.

Sayin ran off to the locker room, and came back to the sideline in a sling. He didn't play the rest of the way.

Sayin went 15-of-29 for 235 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions before he left the game. Sayin has 2,007 passing yards and 19 touchdowns with just four interceptions through seven games this season, his third with the Buckeyes. He was a Heisman finalist last season, too, and finished in fourth in that race.

Luckily for the Buckeyes, they aren't in a rush to figure out their quarterback situation. They are off this week before a matchup against No. 19 USC in Los Angeles on Halloween, so they have some extra time.

Sayin was replaced on Saturday by freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, though he didn't complete either of the two passes he attempted the rest of the way. Indiana had a look to win the game at the end, too, but Nick Marsh's go-ahead touchdown in the final seconds was ruled just out of bounds.

Fahey was a three-star Rivals.com recruit out of high school. He has gone 9-of-13 for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions so far this season, though Saturday was the first meaningful time he's spent on the field. The Buckeyes also have Tavien St. Clair, a sophomore who is a former five-star prospect. St. Clair will presumably back up Fahey against USC, should Day stick with Fahey as his starter.

"I think going into the last few games, Luke's been ahead of Tavien in terms of what we've seen," Day said, via WBNS10 . "But now that we have a bye week, these guys are both going to get a lot of reps … We're going to play the guy that gives us the best chance to win."

Regardless of what plan Day and his staff put together, losing Sayin is a significant blow for the Buckeyes. Replacing him with several big games left on the schedule — including against Oregon, No. 24 Northwestern and Michigan to close out the regular season — and still finding a path to the postseason is not going to be easy.

articles.title: Bayern - Arsenal: Sabor a final en el Allianz
articles.standfirst: Semifinalista y finalista de la pasada edición se citan en el Allianz en uno de los grandes partidos de esta fase liga de la Champions
articles.summary: Semifinalista y finalista de la pasada edición se citan en el Allianz en uno de los grandes partidos de esta fase liga de la Champions
articles.body: La Champions empieza a subir de temperatura. Son partidos correspondientes a la fase liga... pero bien podrían tener como protagonistas a los próximos finalistas que se citarán en la final que tendrá lugar en el Metropolitano el 5 de junio. Esta noche, en el Allianz Arena, se citan el Bayern Múnich, semifinalista de la pasada edición, y un Arsenal que cayó contra el PSG en la final de Budapest. "Para nosotros, se trata de imponer nuestro estilo de juego en el partido. Tenemos que confiar en nuestros principios y en lo que hacemos", expuso Aaron Danks, asistente en el Bayern de un Vincent Kompany que no podrá estar presente en el choque por enfermedad. "Sabemos que el Arsenal es un equipo defensivo fantástico. Será un encuentro de alto nivel. Hay que estar preparado para todo con ellos porque están muy bien entrenados". El Bayern, invicto en el Allianz durante los últimos 39 partidos disputados en fase liga/grupos, necesita reivindicarse tras el 'patinazo' sufrido en su visita al Viking en la segunda jornada. El reto, eso sí, pasa por derrocar a un Arsenal que finalizó con pleno de puntos en la primera fase de la pasada edición, incluida una victoria contra los 'bávaros' en el Emirates, y ha prolongado este estado de forma en la presente imponiéndose a Nápoles y Lille tirando de la unidad 'B'. "Tenemos muchas ganas de que llegue el partido. Este es el tipo de escenario, equipo, entrenador y estadio en el que uno quiere estar. Hemos preparado el partido con mucho entusiasmo", reconoció Arteta en la previa del choque. La motivación sigue intacta tras caer contra el PSG en la final de la pasada edición. "Cuando veo el balón, la música, las escenas, lo quiero tanto… Ese fuego está dentro del equipo y de todos nosotros individualmente". Los 'gunners', que vienen de sacar adelante un partido realmente complicado contra el Nottingham Forest para no perder la estela del Manchester City en Premier, apenas han conseguido ganar en una de sus últimas ocho visitas a Alemania en Europa. Fue contra el Bayer Leverkusen en los dieciseisavos de final de la pasada edición de la Champions. Su última visita al Bayern se saldó con derrota, y eliminación, en la vuelta de los cuartos de final de la Champions. El autor del gol aquella noche fue Kimmich, que "se ausentó del último entrenamiento por motivos personales", Danks no se atrevió a asegurar su presencia en el once de un Bayern que tampoco podrá contar con Michael Olise por sanción. "Karl —reemplazado al descanso contra el Viking— es uno de los muchos que podrían entrar", apuntó Danks. Como alternativa, aparece la figura de un Serge Gnabry que regresa al Emirates... donde llegó a compartir vestuario con Arteta. "Ya era un líder por aquel entonces", exponía el polivalente atacante germano. Queda también la duda sobre la presencia bajo palos de un Manuel Neuer lastrado por unos problemas físicos que le han impedido estar presente en los dos últimos choques. Arteta, por su parte, sigue contando con las bajas de Saliba, Hincapié y Tzolis. Zubimendi, por su parte, ya está recuperado. Más allá de la posible vuelta de Timber al lateral derecho y Lewis-Skelly a la sala de máquinas, el gran quebradero de cabeza está en la banda izquierda. Ante el Nottingham Forest, retiró a Eberechi Eze al descanso para dar entrada a un Noni Madueke que anotó el gol de la victoria. "Tenemos muchos jugadores de gran nivel y las expectativas son muy altas para todos ellos. Queremos más de cada uno. Esa es nuestra mentalidad y eso es lo que nos hará mejorar individualmente y como equipo", alertó Mikel Arteta. Sabe que lo de esta noche en el Allianz es un partido con aroma a final.
