articles.title: Big 12 Commissioner Discusses League's Plans for CFP Expansion, 'We're in the Event Business'
articles.summary: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark told reporters at Big 12 Basketball Media Days on Tuesday that the league would look to replace championship games if the College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams and forces the league to get rid of title contests.
articles.body:
Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark told reporters at Big 12 Basketball Media Days on Tuesday that the league would look to replace championship games if the College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams and forces the league to get rid of title contests.

"First of all, nothing has been done yet with the College Football Playoff. It's only speculation," Yormark told reporters, per ESPN's Myron Medcalf .

"Nothing is final, so I don't want to get too much into the details there, but tentpole events, for us, matter. Our championship game has been very valuable. Our basketball tournament, both men's and women's, has been very valuable. And if there is a point in time where a change is made, we will look to backstop those events with other events. We're in the event business. It drives a lot of fan engagement and excitement, so we'll see what happens in the future, but those are big moments for us. And if for some reason, if one goes away, we'll replace it with something different."

8 Overreactions after Week 7 of CFB Season 😬

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported last Thursday that the CFP is "nearing a deal" that would expand the tournament from 12 to 24 teams in 2027. That deal was expected to happen in the "near future, pending final approvals."

Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger provided more details. In essence, the regular season would end with the last weekend in November. The first weekend in December would include Army-Navy and the Heisman Trophy ceremony, moving those long-storied traditions up on week.

However, with the advent of a 24-team CFP, the postseason needs another week for an extra round that would include eight games involving the No. 8 through No. 24 seeds. The second weekend of December would be reserved for that round.

Put it all together, and there's no spot for conference championship weekend anymore, meaning the elimination of those games.

Dellenger reported "the new expansion contract is expected to soon be signed" after a few college football power brokers had talks with ESPN.

The writing is on the wall here, so if Yormark wants the Big 12 to have a tentpole event, then it'll probably need to be in place by Dec. 2027.

As Medcalf noted, the Big 12 championship game is a big event. Last year's matchup between Texas Tech and BYU (won by the Red Raiders, 34-7) had an attendance of 85,519 at AT&T Stadium, home of the Dallas Cowboys. The game also had an average of 8.99 million viewers (peak of 11.4 million) on ABC, per Jon Lewis of Sports Media Watch .

It's unclear what Yormark might be thinking, but an expanded playoff would certainly help the conference. Of note, in a 24-team format, four more Big 12 teams (BYU, Houston, Arizona and Utah) would have made it last year.

In the meantime, Big 12 football is looking good, especially after BYU beat Notre Dame to move to No. 2 in the polls. Five teams are now in the Top 25, with No. 8 Texas Tech, No. 10 Utah, No. 14 Houston and No. 25 Arizona rounding out the group.

articles.title: Michigan set to start Tommy Carr vs. Indiana after he took over for Bryce Underwood in second half of win over Penn State
articles.summary: The grandson of former Michigan coach Lloyd Carr is the brother of Notre Dame QB CJ Carr.
articles.body:
Tommy Carr is going to get a chance to start against Indiana.

According to multiple reports, the grandson of former Michigan coach Lloyd Carr is set to start for the Wolverines on Saturday. Carr entered the game for Bryce Underwood in the second half of Michigan's 21-18 win over Penn State.

Michigan trailed 3-0 at halftime as Underwood threw an interception when the Wolverines were attempting to get into field goal range before the break. The sophomore was 5-of-11 passing for 43 yards and had two picks.

Carr only threw the ball seven times, but he completed five of those passes for 47 yards. He also rushed four times for 36 yards thanks to a 22-yard run and also scored a touchdown on a 12-yard run that ended up being Michigan's game-winning score after a late Penn State field goal.

A true freshman from Saline, Michigan, Carr is the brother of Notre Dame QB CJ Carr. He was a three-star recruit in the class of 2026 and the No. 37 QB in the country according to Rivals.

If Carr plays well against Indiana, there's no reason to think coach Kyle Whittingham won't give him another opportunity against Rutgers in Week 9. Underwood, a former five-star recruit whose large NIL deal has gotten a lot of scrutiny amid his struggles, is 72-of-124 passing for 924 yards and five touchdowns with six interceptions. He's also taken eight sacks while rushing 60 times for 223 yards and two scores.

Underwood was Michigan's starter as a true freshman in 2025 and completed 60% of his passes for 2,428 yards and 11 TDs with nine interceptions. He also rushed 88 times for 392 yards and six scores. The 2026 season also marks his second offensive system in as many years with the Wolverines. After Sherrone Moore's firing, Michigan hired Whittingham after he parted ways with Utah and Whittingham brought along offensive coordinator Jason Beck.

articles.title: Champions League: Wirtz ends scoring drought as he breaks personal record at Liverpool
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz finally scored his first goal of the season for Liverpool as the Reds beat Villarreal 4-3 to maintain their perfect UEFA Champions League recor...
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz finally scored his first goal of the season for Liverpool as the Reds beat Villarreal 4-3 to maintain their perfect UEFA Champions League record. The Germany international provided assists when Andoni Iraola's side saw off LASK and Brentford in the previous week.

As a result, he has directly contributed to goals in three consecutive games for Liverpool for the very first time. The 23-year-old has consistently faced criticism from all corners for his underwhelming spell at the Merseyside club, but his current form could be a springboard to a more consistent output in the final third.

The former Bayer Leverkusen star replaced Ronald Araujo, who scored Liverpool's second goal as they came from a two-goal deficit, at half-time. Iraola confirmed Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola – who have all joined the club with over €120 million price tag – started the game on the bench for load management reasons.

Wirtz and co. will next face third-placed Brighton at Anfield as Fabian Hürzeler's men will hope to extend their impressive winning streak in Premier League to five games. The 2024/25 champions will then play against Xabi Alonso's Chelsea and the holders Arsenal.

Meanwhile, former Borussia Dortmund attacker Donyell Malen added a goal and an assist to his scintillating stats in 2026 as he helped AS Roma to a 4-0 victory over Slovan Bratislava. Ex-Bayer Leverkusen defender Mario Hermoso opened the scoring for the side from Italy's capital.

Fellow Serie A side Napoli earned their first points of the season with a roller-coaster 4-3 win over Bodø/Glimt, who had the ex-Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Jens Petter Hauge as one of the scorers. Peter Bosz' s PSV also recorded their first win on Tuesday night as former Freiburg striker Guus Til scored the only goal of the game away at Porto.

In the marquee game of the night, the holders PSG maintained their lead at the standings with a 4-2 success over Barcelona. Hansi Flick 's side previously won all of their first 11 games in all competitions.

Despite having to make triple substitutions due to injuries, the Ligue 1 giants repeated their scoreline from Etihad Stadium. Lucas Hernandez , who won the competition with Flick's FC Bayern, scored his first goal since the 2023/24 season. Dani Olmo also suffered an early injury on the day he made his 100th Barcelona appearance.

articles.title: Michigan's Bryce Underwood Benched, Latest Rumors on Wolverines' QB Plans vs. Indiana
articles.summary: Michigan is reportedly changing its starting quarterback for Saturday's game against the reigning national champions.
articles.body:
Michigan is reportedly changing its starting quarterback for Saturday's game against the reigning national champions.

Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reported Tuesday the Wolverines are "expected" to start freshman Tommy Carr against Indiana instead of Bryce Underwood. Carr replaced Underwood during Michigan's most recent game against Penn State and led his team to a 21-18 victory.

To say this is not how Underwood's career with Michigan was expected to unfold would be quite the understatement.

Latest Report Card Grades for Top 20 CFB QBs 🔠

He arrived on campus as the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2025 recruiting class, per 247Sports' composite rankings, and even talked trash to LeBron James about the Ohio State rivalry before he even played a single game.

Underwood was one of the most hyped recruits in recent history, and many Michigan fans surely expected him to lead the team into national championship contention. However, he struggled with consistency as a freshman and ended his first season with 11 touchdown passes to nine interceptions.

He was at his worst in some of the biggest games, including when he went 9-for-24 in a loss to Oklahoma and then failed to back up his words while going 8-of-18 for 63 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception in a loss to the rival Buckeyes.

It wasn't much better to start this season, as Underwood has completed just 58.1 percent of his passes for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions.

Michigan failed to score a single point in the first half of Saturday's game against Penn State, and head coach Kyle Whittingham decided to bench the starting quarterback at halftime after his second interception.

Carr didn't take over from a statistical perspective at 5-of-7 passing for 47 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions, but he ran for 36 yards and a touchdown.

He also avoided the turnovers and costly mistakes that defined Underwood's game and led the team to a comeback win over the Nittany Lions.

Michigan doesn't have much room for error in the College Football Playoff race with a 4-2 record, but Carr will certainly have his chances to make a national statement with challenging games against Indiana, UCLA, Oregon and Ohio State remaining on the slate.

articles.title: “That’s a Really Lame Take”: Kentucky HC Will Stein Defends New 24-Team College Football Playoff Format
articles.summary: As the College Football Playoff is expected to expand from a 12- to 24-team format starting with the 2027 postseason, the college football fraternity seems d...
articles.body:
As the College Football Playoff is expected to expand from a 12- to 24-team format starting with the 2027 postseason, the college football fraternity seems divided on the concept.

One of the biggest areas of concern for those against the expansion is the importance of regular-season matchups. With an increased number of teams set to qualify for the CFP, programs would have a bigger margin of error to play with, which could result in a decrease in the weight of the regular-season games.

However, Will Stein begs to differ. The Kentucky Wildcats coach, according to On3 Sports , defended the proposed expansion, dismissing concerns that a 24-team playoff would reduce the significance of regular-season games.

"Everybody says the (regular season) games aren't going to matter. Really? I think that's a really lame take, to be honest. As far as I know, every game in College Football is going to matter," Stein said. "You telling me you wouldn't want a Playoff game at Kroger Field? I think those takes are bad."

"Everybody says the (regular season) games aren't going to matter. Really? I think that's a really lame take, to be honest. As far as I know, every game in College Football is going to matter," Stein said.

"You telling me you wouldn't want a Playoff game at Kroger Field? I think those takes are bad."

On the field, the Kentucky Wildcats (6-1, 4-1 SEC) are tied for first place in the SEC with No. 5 Georgia (6-1, 4-1) and are ranked No. 12.

ESPN Reportedly Agrees To Pay $345 Million Annually For Expanded CFP

While the college football world argues whether the expansion of the College Football Playoff is the right step for the sport, the format change appears to be a major financial deal for college football.

With reports of a handshake agreement between CFP and ESPN to broadcast the 24-team playoff format starting in 2027, Pete Thamel reported that ESPN will pay the CFP $345 million annually for the next five years. However, ESPN will earn back $140 million due to the cancellation of three power conference championship game agreements.

These annual broadcasting fees will be paid on top of a $1.3 billion sum that the network is already slated to pay the CFP as part of its existing college football broadcasting rights.

articles.title: UND cornerback Grant Noland drawing attention as FCS leader in pass break-ups
articles.summary: Oct. 20—GRAND FORKS — After the UND football team upset then-No. 1 South Dakota State last Saturday, Fighting Hawks linebacker Mike Devereaux gave a shoutout...
articles.body:
Oct. 20—GRAND FORKS — After the UND football team upset then-No. 1 South Dakota State last Saturday, Fighting Hawks linebacker Mike Devereaux gave a shoutout to cornerback Grant Noland.

"Grant Noland is one of the best corners in the nation," Devereaux said. "I feel like a lot of attention needs to be brought to him."

Noland was named this week's Missouri Valley Football Conference Defensive Player of the Week after registering a career-high six pass break-ups against SDSU. The six pass break-ups are the most by an FCS or FBS player in a game this season.

Noland and the defense limited the nation's second-highest scoring offense to a season-low 10 points and 326 yards of total offense.

Noland, a Kearney, Mo., native, took over the FCS lead in total pass break-ups, increasing his total to 13. UND's all-time single-season record, which includes postseason statistics, is 15 — set by Dustin Thornburg during UND's run to the NCAA Division II national championship in 2001.

Noland comes from a football family with some UND roots. His grandpa, Terry Noland, was UND's defensive coordinator for three seasons until 1983.

Terry Noland left UND for Central Missouri in 1983, bringing with him UND offensive coordinator Rob Bollinger, who would return to UND when Roger Thomas took over for Pat Behrns in 1986.

From 1983 to 1996, Terry Noland posted a 78-65-2 record at Central Missouri. He owns the school record for wins and conference titles. The football offices at Central Missouri are named after him.

Grant's dad, Erek Noland, was a defensive back at Wyoming from 1992-95.

"The only thing Grant does better than covering guys is hunting, and that's why he loves Grand Forks," UND head coach Eric Schmidt said. "He's a quiet assassin. I love that kid. He runs really, really well. Tackles well. Every single day we talk about being consistently good over occasionally great. He is consistently good. What you saw (Saturday) is the same thing we'll get on Tuesday. He's really honest with himself, too. He's a good self-assessor."

Noland was recruited to Grand Forks as a safety but moved to cornerback, partly due to injuries at the position in 2025. He made nine starts last season as a true freshman and earned Freshman All-America honors by Phil Steele and FCS Football Central. He ended the year with 48 tackles and one pass break-up.

Noland spent this fall camp battling 1-on-1 often with UND wide receiver Deng Deng, a physical 6-foot-4 wide receiver.

"It's huge when you have those opportunities in practice," Schmidt said. "That's how you get better. He never gets too high. He doesn't get too low. He's really humble. He wants to get better, and he doesn't panic when he's out there. You never see him really out of position all that much. He does a great job fitting routes with his eyes, and then fitting with his body, as well. He just has a really good feel and timing mechanism to be able to play the ball at the right time. I think what's impressive with all the pass break-ups is he doesn't have a lot of penalties against him. So to be able to play that way and play clean, I think says something about what an elite corner looks like."

articles.title: 'Los Cuatro Magníficos' del Feyenoord examinan al Betis: Zechiël, Ferri, Moussa y Valente
articles.standfirst: Entre los cuatro han 'fabricado' 22 de los 35 goles que acumulan los de Van Bronckhorst
articles.summary: Entre los cuatro han 'fabricado' 22 de los 35 goles que acumulan los de Van Bronckhorst
articles.body: El 'Spanish' Feyenoord de Mika Mármol, Javi López y Nacho Ferri -rival del Betis- aterriza en La Cartuja en uno de los mejores momentos de su historia reciente. Los de Giovanni van Bronckhorst, que ya hizo campeón de Liga al conjunto de Róterdam en la 2016-17, llegan como líderes en solitario de la Eredivisie. Aventajan en tres puntos al AZ Alkmaar, en cuatro al PSV y en cinco al Ajax después de sumar 23 de los 27 puntos en disputa. No sólo eso. Los 31 goles que acumulan en nueve jornadas son su segundo mejor registro anotador desde la 1974-75, sólo superados por las 32 dianas que sumaban, a estas alturas, con Arne Slot en la 2023-24. Un 'clímax' alimentado con su victoria en Champions sobre el Como (3-2) y por el gran momento que atraviesan sus 'Cuatro Magníficos'. Gjivai Zechiël, Nacho Ferri y Anis Hadj Moussa -los tres están empatados a seis goles- y el capitán Luciano Valente han hecho olvidar a la venta al Lille de Ayase Ueda, 'Pichichi' de la pasada Eredivisie con 25 dianas. Nacho Ferri (Montaverner, 2004) ha caído de pie en De Kuip. El atacante español, fichado del Westerlo este verano a cambio de 9 millones, está de dulce. Puede presumir de ser el primer jugador del Feyenoord que está involucrado en, al menos un gol, en sus primeros cinco partidos como titular con el Feyenoord en la Eredivisie. Sus 192 centímetros son 'oro' para los de Róterdam. "Es bueno como delantero centro, pero también puede usar su velocidad para aprovechar los espacios a la espalda de la defensa", asegura Gio van Bronckhorst al referirse al español, que acumula seis goles y una asistencia en los 10 partidos (557') que ha disputado. Dicho de otro modo: participa en un gol cada 69'. Gjivai Zechiël (Róterdam, 2004) ha regresado al Feyenoord por la 'puerta grande'. El '8' completó con nota su cesión al Utrecht. Registró 10 goles y 10 asistencias en 50 partidos. Este curso va por el mismo camino. Es el centrocampista de las grandes Ligas que ha 'fabricado' más goles (10): ha marcado seis y ha asistido en cuatro. Su condición de 'box-to-box' y el dinamismo que aporta con su ida y vuelta desde el rol de interior ha convencido también a Xavi Hernández, que le hizo debutar en el parón con Países Bajos. "Soy fan suyo", dijo el ex del Barcelona. "Casi no pierde balones, ve las jugadas rápidamente y es capaz de ejecutarlas”, asegura Ron Jans, su exentrenador en el Utrecht. Anis Hadj Moussa (París, 2002) es el futbolista 'diferente' del Feyenoord de mediocampo en adelante. "Es un jugador diferencial. Todavía no tenemos jugadores como él, que marquen la diferencia en este nivel", reconocía Cesc Fàbregas después de que el internacional argelino marcara un gol y provocara otro en la victoria sobre el Como (3-2). "Anis es, sencillamente, un jugador de primer nivel, un artista. Estamos muy contentos de poder contar con él este año", apunta Van Bronckhorst para referirse a su plasticidad y facilidad para el regate. Con Givairo Read forma una conexión muy potente por derecha. El lateral aporta profundidad y eso permite a Hadj Moussa, zurdo a banda cambiada, pisar zonas interiores. En total, registra seis goles y dos asistencias este curso. Luciano Valente (Groningen, 2003) es, junto a Sem Steijn, el líder espiritual de este Feyenoord. De ahí que luzca el brazalete de capitán. El internacional neerlandés destaca por su capacidad para incorporarse al ataque con el balón controlado y por su 'timing' para llegar desde segunda línea. Además, lanza penaltis. "Cada vez que el Feyenoord ataca, espero que le pasen el balón a Valente. Da unos pases preciosos y hace que parezca facilísimo. Disfruto muchísimo viéndolo jugar", apunta Bram van Polen, exjugador del PEC Zwolle. "Destacaría su disposición, tanto con balón como sin él, su buena técnica para encontrar soluciones hacia delante y su capacidad para encontrar jugadores entre líneas", sugiere Ronald Koeman. El Betis ya sabe lo que le espera.

articles.title: El 'top-8' del Atlético pasa por ganar ‘casi’ todo
articles.standfirst: Tras dejarse cinco puntos en dos salidas, los rojiblancos, que se quejan de un penalti sobre Hancko, se jugarán parte de sus opciones la próxima jornada... ante el Bayern
articles.summary: Tras dejarse cinco puntos en dos salidas, los rojiblancos, que se quejan de un penalti sobre Hancko, se jugarán parte de sus opciones la próxima jornada... ante el Bayern
articles.body: La racha imponente de seis victorias se acabó. Quizá en el momento que más necesitaba el Atlético para aclarar de manera notable el panorama rumbo al top-8, objetivo de los de Simeone para evitar ese cruce anterior a octavos que pone en peligro la Champions... y que obliga a los del Metropolitano a dejar escapar pocos puntos más. Cinco, de hecho, han volado en este arranque de la fase de grupos.Cinco (tres en Anfield, dos en Stuttgart) que convierten los cinco partidos que restan en auténticas finales. En especial, el siguiente choque del grupo, una visita del Bayern Múnich que, de no ganar, pondrá el panorama muy complicado pese a que las últimas cuatro jornadas el calendario se suaviza de una manera evidente. Un traspiés que, quizá, es menor al jugar la última media hora con 10 jugadores. Uno menos por una jugada fuera de foco de unHjulmand que fue ‘reprendido’ por el propio Simeone a la hora de valorar una acción de “tirarse al piso” que acabó frenando la evidente remontada rojiblanca.Pasó de una primera parte superado claramente a igualar la contienda en el cuarto de hora del arranque del segundo acto.Pero llegó la roja del danés... y todo cambió. Una acción que condicionó el partido, pero no fue la única polémica del partido.De hecho, Grimaldo puso el foco en una acción que, entiende el lateral, debió ser penalti a favor por una entrada a Hancko. “Ha habido un penalti clarísimo que no entiendo que el VAR entre en algunas situaciones, no entre en otras. Es algo que no termino de entender, pero creo que en la tele todo el mundo lo ha podido ver”, comentó Grimaldo sobre la jugada que, entienden en el Atlético. El ex del Bayer Leverkusen siguió insistiendo en una acción en la que Simeone no quiso entrar: “Es una jugada que tenemos para él al primer palo y le chafan ahí. Es un penalti clarísimo. Hace poco nos pitaron a nosotros un penalti en una falta lateral, ahora no lo pitan. Supongo que tendrán que salir a dar alguna explicación”. “Yo lo veo, yo soy el que saca el córner. Le pisan y va al suelo. Yo creo que ni lo han parado a mirar. No entendemos que no lo miren. Necesitamos que den explicaciones. Saber el motivo por el que unas veces entran y otras no”, zanjó Grimaldo sobre una acción que, de haber sido pitada, habría condicionado el resultado tanto como la de Hjulmand. Sea como fuere, el Atlético rompe una racha de triunfos y vuelve a demostrar que su buen momento en LaLiga fuera de casa (cuatro triunfos de cinco partidos) no tiene continuación en Champions, donde ha sido incapaz de vencer tanto en el campo del Liverpool como en el del Stuttgart. Se acabó el margen para no poner en riesgo meterse entre los ocho primeros de esta fase de grupos de la competición.

articles.title: El Atleti se aletarga y Julián despierta
articles.standfirst: En copa de balón
articles.summary: En copa de balón
articles.body: La Champions no perdona la somnolencia. Acunado en seis victorias consecutivas, el Atlético llegó a Stuttgart con el estómago lleno y pagó caro su adormecimiento en el primer tiempo. El equipo del Cholo no parecía un equipo de Simeone y se dejó las credenciales en el vestuario. Los gestos de desesperación del entrenador eran ostensibles. El Stuttgart apretó la salida de balón de Llorente y Pubill, que durante un buen rato no ejercieron de campeones del mundo. Que dos de los jugadores más fiables del fútbol español naufragaran así resume el mal primer tiempo de un equipo al que le costó media hora entender que la música de la Liga de Campeones no tolera semejante falta de tensión. El gol del Stuttgart llegó en ese tramo y hasta se quedó corto. Oblak, en versión de sus mejores tiempos, fue otra vez el mejor de los suyos y mantuvo el barco a flote cuando solo había agua que achicar. La ‘Cholina’ debió de ser de época al descanso, porque el equipo que no negocia el esfuerzo se había dedicado a racanear. No fue lo único en lo que acertó Simeone. Lookman entró por Jonathan David y tardó un minuto en sacar a Julián Alvarez de su letargo. El nigeriano dio un pase al corazón del área y con el paso atrás del gran delantero que es, Julián la puso en la escuadra y el notición quedó servido: el argentino se reencontró con el gol, que es el camino más corto para reencontrarse con su afición. El empate lo cambiaba todo. Llegaron entonces los mejores minutos del Atlético, que empezó a hallar espacios y a empequeñecer al buen equipo alemán. Hasta que Hjulmand, que tiene un máster en pasarse de frenada, le complicó la vida a su equipo con una roja de libro. Agarrado al empate y con el espíritu recobrado, el Atleti supo aguantar sin sufrir lo indecible. Pudo haber pasado de la siesta a la fiesta si el danés no hubiese metido la pata. Por cómo empezó, el punto vale. Por cómo estaba cambiando el partido, deja un regusto agridulce, pero empatar jugando mal también es cosa de equipos grandes.

articles.title: Real Madrid - RB Leipzig: Vini busca brillar antes del apagón
articles.standfirst: Sancionado en Liga hasta finales de noviembre, el brasileño afronta ante el Leipzig su última ventana para reivindicarse antes de desaparecer dos semanas
articles.summary: Sancionado en Liga hasta finales de noviembre, el brasileño afronta ante el Leipzig su última ventana para reivindicarse antes de desaparecer dos semanas
articles.body: Pocos futbolistas saben tanto como Vinicius de vivir en el ojo del huracán. Esta vez, sin embargo, el vendaval le sopla de cara. El brasileño llega al duelo ante el Leipzig atravesando quizá su tramo más espeso desde que es madridista. Castigado en Liga hasta finales de noviembre, señalado por su bajón futbolístico y con un puesto que se le resquebraja bajo los pies. El Bernabéu, en Champions, es la tabla a la que agarrarse. El calendario le aprieta como un cepo. Tras medirse al Leipzig, Vinicius se esfumará del itinerario competitivo hasta el 4 de noviembre, cuando el Madrid visite al AEK de Atenas en la cuarta jornada europea. Y aún le quedará un impás pendiente en Liga. Concretamente un partido de sanción que se jugará en Mestalla, el estadio que lo recibe siempre a dentelladas y que ya se perdió la temporada pasada, aquella vez por ciclo de amarillas. La paz con su propia grada, además, apenas había empezado a cuajar. El Bernabéu la había tomado con él en varios pasajes de esta temporada, y en el partido del Villarreal parecía amainar el runrún, hasta que la noche se torció. Vinicius vio la roja por el tirón de pelo a Saliba, pidió perdón en redes y volvió a quedar en el centro de la diana. En Roma, encima, firmó una de sus peores versiones. No desequilibró en ataque y erró en los metros decisivos de varias jugadas, con un colofón amargo: en el 2-1 romano, un taconazo fallido en el centro del campo abrió la autopista del contragolpe que acabó en gol. Mourinho no lo encajó bien, lo sustituyó y replicó el gesto desde la banda, un reproche que terminó aislado con el pasar de los días entre el técnico y su estrella. Y mientras Vinicius se apaga, otro se enciende en su territorio. Diomande fue uno de los que volteó la segunda parte en Roma, firmó un golazo y una asistencia ante el Sevilla y una semana antes había resuelto el partido del Villarreal con un tanto solitario. Cada destello del marfileño engorda las dudas sobre esa banda izquierda que Vinicius gobernaba sin discusión, un trono que ahora tiene inquilinos a la espera. Si a eso se suman el momento de Güler y el rompecabezas que plantea la posición de Valverde, la situación se complica para el brasileño. Mourinho, además, se encargó de retirar cualquier red de seguridad bajo los pies del brasileño. Preguntado en la previa por si Vinicius es intocable, el técnico fue tajante: “Intocable es el escudo. No me gusta este concepto de jugador intocable”. El portugués dinamitó la idea de que la jerarquía blinde un puesto: “Lo que convierte a los jugadores en intocables no es el estatus, ni el brazalete, ni los años que lleva en el club. Tampoco cuánto se ha pagado por él. Lo que hace a un jugador intocable es su rendimiento en el campo”. Por eso la cita de esta noche sabe a examen. Vinicius necesita un chispazo de los suyos, de esos que recuerdan por qué fue durante años el jugador más determinante del equipo, antes de ceder su protagonismo a la oscuridad del calendario. Dos semanas sin él darán tiempo de sobra para que otros ocupen su espacio. Brillar hoy es su manera de dejar la luz encendida antes de su apagón.

articles.title: David Sánchez no tiene dudas con el Clásico: "El Real Madrid no es, ni por asomo, algo parecido al PSG"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco defiende al Barcelona pese a su derrota ante el PSG y asegura que el conjunto blanco está muy lejos del nivel de los parisinos
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco defiende al Barcelona pese a su derrota ante el PSG y asegura que el conjunto blanco está muy lejos del nivel de los parisinos
articles.body: La derrota del FC Barcelona ante el PSG (4-2) en el Parque de los Príncipes no ha sembrado las dudas en David Sánchez. El periodista, en su opinión en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, reconoció la superioridad del conjunto dirigido por Luis Enrique, pero quiso dejar claro que el equipo de Hansi Flick sigue siendo perfectamente capaz de imponerse al Real Madrid en el próximo Clásico. "El Barcelona perdió mereciendo perder ante el mejor equipo del mundo, el PSG de Luis Enrique Martínez, que es, sin duda, el máximo favorito a volver por tercera vez consecutiva a ganar la Liga de Campeones", comenzó señalando David Sánchez, que, pese al resultado, defendió la actuación de los azulgranas. "El partido del Barcelona no fue tan malo como muchos están diciendo. Estuvo mucho mejor el Barcelona ayer, palmando 4-2, que en aquella famosa derrota ante el PSG en Barcelona por 1-2, donde los de Luis Enrique Martínez vapulearon y bailaron al FC Barcelona", explicó. El periodista también reconoció que el conjunto de Flick tiene aspectos que corregir, aunque insistió en la dificultad del rival: "¿Qué hay cosas a mejorar? Evidentemente, sí. Ayer te enfrentabas al mejor equipo de Europa en su casa y lo normal es perder". Sin embargo, el mensaje más contundente de David Sánchez llegó al analizar el próximo enfrentamiento contra el Real Madrid de José Mourinho. El periodista considera que las diferencias entre el conjunto blanco y el PSG son enormes y que el Barcelona no tendrá que afrontar las mismas dificultades. "Pero ninguna duda con este equipo respecto a lo que pueda pasar en el Clásico. El Real Madrid no es, ni por asomo, algo parecido al PSG. Ni robarán el balón tan arriba como lo hace el conjunto parisino, ni tendrá jamás el control del partido el equipo de José Mourinho", aseguró. David Sánchez fue incluso más allá y se mostró convencido de que el Barcelona, manteniendo el nivel exhibido en París, sería capaz de superar al conjunto madridista: "Creo que jugando los mismos jugadores que jugaron ayer en el Parque de los Príncipes y al mismo nivel rindiendo el domingo, ganarían con facilidad al equipo de Mourinho". Para terminar, el periodista reafirmó su confianza en Hansi Flick y sus futbolistas, aunque admitió que todavía existe una diferencia respecto al vigente referente europeo: "Ni una sola duda con el equipo de Flick, que ayer confirmó lo que muchos ya sabíamos, que todavía no están al nivel del mejor equipo del mundo, el PSG de Luis Enrique Martínez".

articles.title: Como vs Man Utd: Cesc Fabregas prepares for Champions League clash as Ludi reflects on club's rise and Bruno Fernandes reunion
articles.summary: Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi explains Cesc Fabregas' impact on the club's rise to the Champions League; Ludi reflects on his time playing alongside a teenage Bruno Fernandes at Novara ahead of Manchester United's visit.
articles.body:
The club's journey from Italy's lower leagues to Serie A and Champions League qualification is an extraordinary story. Yet what makes it so compelling is the speed of their progress, combined with a determination to establish themselves as a force in Italian football for years to come.

In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News , Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi reflects on the club's transformation, the influence of head coach Cesc Fabregas and an unlikely reunion with Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes.

'Fabregas the driving force behind Como's rise'

To understand Como's recent history, look at the transformation since Fabregas joined the club in 2022.

The former Spain international arrived towards the end of his playing career, with Como in Serie B. He subsequently retired, joined the club's academy coaching staff and eventually became head coach of the senior team.

In the four years since his arrival, Fabregas has helped Como secure promotion to Serie A for the first time in 21 years before guiding them to Champions League qualification last season for the first time in the club's history.

Ludi believes the Spaniard's influence extends far beyond the pitch.

"Cesc made a big difference. Not only on the field, but also off the field, in my opinion - the culture of the club, everything. The professionalism, everything, to be honest," he said.

"He brought his mentality into the club and that's one of the reasons why we improved and grew so quickly. Thanks to him, we are fantastic, to be honest.

"We have been fantastic on the field, but thanks to him we also improved our mentality, so we were ready to compete for the Champions League."

Fabregas' presence was evident at his news conference ahead of Como's meeting with Manchester United. Sitting alongside summer signing Nico Paz, he fielded questions on a range of subjects, including whether he could one day become United's head coach.

The composure with which he handled the questions reflected the authority he has established at Como. While the word 'aura' is often overused in football, it is difficult to ignore the impact Fabregas has made on the club.

Ludi is particularly impressed by the 39-year-old's willingness to keep learning.

"He's very young, but he's so open-minded, to be honest. He's the first who wants to improve and learn," he said.

"That, in my opinion, is one of his best qualities and he's making a difference.

"Our team is Cesc Fabregas on the field. Courage, intelligence, talent, talented players. We are trying to do the same with our team. The way Cesc is and the way Cesc was as a footballer is what we want to be as a team."

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Ludi share a similar journey through Italian football, having both experienced the climb from Serie B towards the Champions League.

The pair shared a dressing room at Novara when Fernandes was just 17, with Ludi serving as his captain as the teenager began his professional career.

Asked what the young Fernandes was like, Ludi smiled before describing him as "phenomenal".

Fernandes went on to play for Udinese and Sampdoria before moving to Sporting Lisbon and eventually Manchester United. Ludi, however, still remembers the teenager who is now set to lead United against Como.

"I'm really happy to speak about Bruno," Ludi said.

"We met each other when he was a kid, literally a kid. He was a kid in a professional environment, so he probably wasn't ready to join a professional environment.

"At the beginning, I needed to guide him in our dressing room in order for him to understand what being a professional meant.

"But then, to be honest, it was fantastic because I met a fantastic guy, a humble person, a top footballer, but an open-minded guy, always ready to support, ready to help, ready to enjoy, ready to have fun with all of us.

"He's a very nice guy, so I was so happy and I always celebrated his improvement because he deserves it.

"I imagine it'll be nice to see him, maybe after the game, but to be honest, it would be fantastic to meet him in the Champions League. It's something I never expected, and it would be just fantastic.

"It was just one season but a great season for all of us, and I think that I met one of the best people I've ever met in my life."

There have been defining moments in Como's recent history, not least the draw against Cosenza in May 2024 that secured the point they needed for promotion to Serie A.

That achievement laid the foundations for the club's subsequent rise to the Champions League. But hosting Manchester United represents another landmark in a journey that has exceeded expectations.

Spending time around the club in the build-up to the game, the excitement is palpable. There is a sense of disbelief, pride and appreciation at the prospect of welcoming Michael Carrick's United side.

For Ludi, who joined Como in 2019, the scale of the transformation is particularly striking.

"Yeah, it's incredible, to be honest," he said.

"I started to work here in 2019 and there was nothing.

"Now we have the Champions League, we have Man Utd at home, and it's something that is amazing, literally amazing.

"Sometimes it's good to look behind, because sometimes we forget what we did. In football, every day there is something to achieve, there is a reason to step forward.

"I don't want to be arrogant, but we are here to write the history of Como, and this is another page, a big page of our history.

"We want our fans to be proud of us and we want to compete, to fight, in order to write another page. First of all, it will be another nice page in the history of Como."

articles.title: Foden shines as Man City rout Athens 5-1 despite Haaland, Semenyo injuries
articles.summary: Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City bounced back from last week’s loss to PSG despite off-field troubles.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca believes Phil Foden has provided evidence that his prolonged slump might finally be over by scoring a hat-trick in Manchester City’s 5-1 rout of AEK Athens in the Champions League.

After struggling badly over the last two seasons, England playmaker Foden could be on the brink of a long-awaited renaissance after his sublime display at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday.

It has been a trying period for the 26-year-old, who has admitted suffering from mental health issues.

Foden fell out of favour with former City boss Pep Guardiola and had not scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s Premier League win against Ipswich.

This season has been another turbulent experience for Foden, who was sent off in City’s win at Manchester United and has been forced to battle for a place in Maresca’s starting lineup.

Taking advantage of injuries that left Erling Haaland on the bench against AEK and sidelined Antoine Semenyo for eight weeks, Foden starred on the left wing before switching to the “false nine” role as the focal point of City’s attack.

“It is good news for me because you know he is doing well and this is what we want for many reasons,” City boss Maresca said.

“First of all, because he is a top player and we know that. Happy for him, but also happy for the team that we have one more weapon that we can use.”

Foden’s hat-trick will surely have caught England manager Thomas Tuchel’s eye as he prepares to pick his squad for the Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain in November.

Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace.

Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to earn the trust of Maresca and Tuchel.

articles.title: Real Madrid veteran expected to return to starting XI against RB Leipzig – Report
articles.summary: Real Madrid are preparing to face RB Leipzig in the Champions League as they look to continue their perfect record in the tournament.Jose Mourinho is unlikel...
articles.body:
Real Madrid are preparing to face RB Leipzig in the Champions League as they look to continue their perfect record in the tournament.

Jose Mourinho is unlikely to make many changes to the starting line-up against the Bundesliga club despite an El Clasico ahead of them.

Now, according to Diario AS , Antonio Rudiger is expected to return to Real Madrid's starting line-up for their game against Leipzig.

Mourinho is planning to put the veteran defender alongside Ibrahima Konate in the back line as he looks to get his structure right.

Rudiger and Konate expected to lead Madrid's defence

Rudiger has been rotating with Dean Huijsen in central defence, but the German is now tipped to reclaim his starting position for the European fixture.

Konate, meanwhile, is expected to retain his place, setting up an experienced and physically imposing partnership.

The game also carries additional significance for the French international, who previously represented Leipzig before joining Liverpool in 2021.

Antonio Rudiger has been rotating with Dean Huijsen for minutes. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

Denzel Dumfries is considered the favourite to start at right-back, while Marc Cucurella is expected to occupy the opposite flank.

With Thibaut Courtois behind them, Madrid could field a defensive unit combining physical strength, experience and attacking support from the full-back positions.

Rudiger's expected return gives Mourinho another opportunity to assess his preferred defensive combinations before facing Barcelona.

His aggression in individual duels and ability to defend physically could prove valuable against Leipzig's attacking players.

Konate offers similar strengths, particularly when covering space behind the defensive line. Together, they should be able to hold the fort against the German club.

Ibrahima Konate will come face-to-face with his former club tonight. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

However, their partnership will also need to demonstrate coordination in possession and the ability to play out from the back.

That becomes especially relevant ahead of the Clasico , where Barcelona's movement between the lines and pace in wide areas will demand constant concentration.

Mourinho's decision to start them together tonight could give him a clearer idea of whether to retain the partnership against Barça and play one of them alongside Dean Huijsen.

The priority for Madrid is to secure a victory against RB Leipzig, but the Barça game would also be on Mourinho's mind, and it remains to be seen how the duo fare.

articles.title: Colin Kazim-Richards: Crawley Town sack head coach after poor start
articles.summary: Crawley Town sack head coach Colin Kazim-Richards with the side five points adrift at the bottom of League Two.
articles.body:
Crawley Town have sacked head coach Colin Kazim-Richards with the side five points adrift at the bottom of League Two.

Kazim-Richards was dismissed after his side's 3-2 loss at home to Shrewsbury Town on Tuesday night.

It was their seventh loss in 10 league games - the Red Devils have won just once in League Two all season.

Kazim-Richards' assistant Julian Gray has also been relieved of his duties while director of football Erdem Konyar will leave the club too.

"The club would like to place on record its sincere thanks to Colin and Julian, who joined during a challenging period and played an important role in securing the club's EFL status at the end of last season," a club statement read. , external

"We would also like to thank Erdem for his hard work and commitment since returning to the club last year.

"All three depart with the best wishes of everyone at Crawley Town, and we wish them every success in their future endeavours."

articles.title: Erik ten Hag interview: Man Utd's use of data, impact of legends’ criticism, and ‘special’ Mainoo
articles.summary: This is part two of The Athletic’s interview with former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag, now the technical director of FC Twente in the Netherlands
articles.body:
Soon after, he pulls up in a silver Range Rover and gets out to exchange a handshake. He has finished a day's work at FC Twente's stadium, De Grolsch Veste, where he is technical director.

A short while later, he is driving us through picturesque Dutch countryside on the way to Ros van Twente, the hotel he co-owns with his brothers, Michel and Rico, and John Berghaan and Anita Stappenbeld, who run it. "They got married two weeks ago as a surprise," says Ten Hag, grinning.

Two years on from the end of his time in charge of Manchester United , Ten Hag is in a relaxed mood. As we weave through the flat fields, he provides a history of the place. "The Germans were here in the Second World War, but also the English and Americans afterwards - they lived here on the base of the military airport," he says.

Heaven is a Place on Earth by Belinda Carlisle comes out of the speakers as his car stereo goes through a 1980s playlist. "In this period it was real music; now everything is computer," he adds.

He moves on to a devastating event in the year 2000 that affected him while playing for FC Twente. A fireworks depot that supplied pop concerts exploded, killing 23 people, including four firefighters, injuring 950, and destroying 400 homes. Ten Hag says it was lucky the blast didn't hit the propane drums at the Grolsch brewing factory on the outskirts of town; otherwise, the damage would have been even more severe.

Twente's training ground was close by and players' families and friends were hurt, but the club ordered the squad to complete their final match of the season the next day, a trip to Feyenoord. Afterwards, Ten Hag gave an interview to broadcast media and criticised the executives.

"The leadership of the club were mad at me, but they had made the decision to play," explains Ten Hag. "Everyone is agreeing now: you can't play football when your city is burning."

Ten Hag speaking his mind is a theme that comes up repeatedly as we talk in a private dining room at the hotel. He opens up like never before on many key aspects of his time in charge of Manchester United and his career since, including:

The use of data at United and his offer to INEOS

Why a 2-2 draw with Sevilla in April 2023 was a turning point in his reign

How that summer's pre-season 'killed' players

The rationale of picking Noussair Mazraoui at No 10 in Istanbul

How players are affected by United legends who are now pundits

His 'strange' three-game spell at Bayer Leverkusen

In January 2023, Ten Hag needed a replacement for Cristiano Ronaldo at centre-forward. He used his Dutch connections to loan Wout Weghorst from Burnley, and to this day feels the striker's work off the ball was a contributing factor in Marcus Rashford hitting 30 goals that season.

"Wout did well for us; what he took out of his career is amazing," says Ten Hag. "Like Marcel Sabitzer. We got success, winning the League Cup, third position; we were a team because they worked hard. Wout was one of the reasons Rashford was so important."

Weghorst, standing at 6ft 6in (198cm), made an unexpected appearance as a No 10 in the Camp Nou, where Rashford went up top and scored in a 2-2 draw against Barcelona. United came from behind to win 2-1 in the home leg, a last-32 tie in the Europa League, one of the great recent European nights at Old Trafford.

Weghorst then started up top in the Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United at Wembley, sliding a pass through to Rashford, who finished to make the score 2-0.

A week later, United got thumped 7-0 at Anfield.

"The team was not consistent," says Ten Hag. "On our good day we could match the best teams in the league, in the world, I would even say. On the worst day, we sat below the bottom. And then in Liverpool, obviously, we went below the bottom, also mentality-wise. It was the next Premier League game after we won the League Cup. We were on the high; we went up there, maybe we were too confident, and we got punished. Every attack was a goal."

But the game in which Ten Hag feels his reign changed was the quarter-final of the Europa League a month later, when United were knocked out 5-2 on aggregate by Sevilla, having been 2-0 up in the first leg. "The team couldn't play without two players," he says, naming Lisandro Martinez (Licha) and Bruno Fernandes.

"Licha was so important for us to play from the back, but also the winning mentality, winning duels. And Bruno. In that game (first leg), at 2-0 up, I decided to sub Bruno, 30 minutes from time, and then Lisandro broke his foot."

United finished the season with 27 home wins, equalling a club record across a campaign, but they would have broken it had they held on at Old Trafford against Sevilla.

Ten Hag had shown his faith in Fernandes by naming him captain. "I think it was good for the team, the best solution, and for him it was good as well. Obviously he has some pros and cons, but he has great game understanding, he's a top professional, and he always gives his best; lifestyle good. Every day, he goes to the limit; he's driving it."

Ten Hag laughs. "Sometimes he's getting emotional, but he's a winner."

Ten Hag allowed Fernandes tactical latitude on the pitch. "I gave him some freedom in the game plan. I think I'm always quite self-critical and reflective. I have to say I can't see a game where the players didn't want to transfer the game plan onto the pitch. They were always trying because I think they believed in what we did."

Pre-season before the 2023-24 season , during which United flew to New Jersey, San Diego, Houston and Las Vegas, pointed at issues ahead. Flying 13,650 miles across the Atlantic, from city to city, impacted the players, Ten Hag reveals.

"The tour was so much expectation on the players," he says. "We got exhausted from all the kilometres. We started in New York, we played in Houston, we played in Vegas, went back, we gave them a couple of days off, and then we didn't train proper tactical and physical work for 10 days because they were totally killed… We were never fit."

Kobbie Mainoo, then 18, suffered an ankle injury against Real Madrid in Texas. When he finally made his first Premier League start, at Everton, he was named man of the match in a 3-0 win.

Ten Hag knew he had struck gold from the academy when he was first drawn to Mainoo in July 2022. "The first time I saw him, playing for the second team, I thought, 'OK, he's an amazing talent'. But he was too easy. I saw that we needed him to get in a higher intensity. We started to bring him in drills where we challenged him on dynamics."

Mainoo has recently praised the sessions put on by Ten Hag and his assistant, Mitchell van der Gaag. He told Clarence Seedorf on Amazon Prime how training was "tough" but among "the best" of his career, adding: "The intensity and competitiveness of those sessions really helped me in that time."

Ten Hag laughs. He gets sent all the quotes from players criticising his regime, but this is one that hasn't been passed on to him. "Kobbie is, for me, special. A lot of people were building him, supporting him. But in the end, he's doing it by himself."

United's injuries continued that season, though, and results suffered. Ten Hag picked 13 different centre-back combinations and changed his back four 29 times. "So it's almost impossible to get automatism in," he says. "But I know at the top, it's about the result."

Ten Hag adds: "Expectations at United are so huge, everyone is expecting the team to win the league every year. But be fair, United at that time, and also definitely two years after, are not able to win the league.

"We could have won the title if we had continued on building. But in that time we were not consistent enough; the squad was not good enough to win it."

'Sancho didn't want to play on the right'

In October 2024, United's executives decided Ten Hag was not the man to lead them to a title challenge. The writing appeared on the wall after his job was so publicly at risk around the FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City five months earlier. But he insists his maverick choice to start Mazraoui at No 10 at Fenerbahce in his penultimate game was not a last roll of the dice, but rather a selection Jose Mourinho would not predict.

"Not everything comes out in Carrington," says Ten Hag, chuckling about news leaking from United's training ground. "That's me; I surprised them also in the FA Cup final, and often I got it right. That's not a risk to put Mazraoui there… But sometimes I have to go more in the head of a fan or media, to think that they think it's weird. For me, it was logic."

Ten Hag started loanee Sofyan Amrabat in the FA Cup final against Manchester City, instead of Casemiro, to get more coverage in midfield. United then bought Manuel Ugarte that summer but Ten Hag thinks he could have instead kept Scott McTominay and saved money on Amrabat. He says: "I wanted to keep Sofyan Amrabat, they didn't. I think he did a great job at United."

Ten Hag was scrutinised by pundits for his call in Istanbul, and for much else in his tenure, but he has a sanguine response to a question about the impact on United of the host of former players giving their views as pundits. Gary Neville, Roy Keane, Wayne Rooney, Rio Ferdinand, Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt all regularly pass comment, occasionally sharply, on their YouTube shows as well as more mainstream channels.

"It's everywhere the same; they always want to protect their legacies," says Ten Hag. "It's no different than Bayern Munich or Ajax; they do the same. But they are (part of United's) history, and they do not always know what's going on. Football evolves. For United, it's clear: they had great contributions, they achieved massive results, trophies for the club and for themselves, so I respect them.

"I have to say, I had a very good relationship with them all, with Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand. I did nice interviews with them both, so it didn't hurt me. Of course, they have podcasts, they have their models. Sometimes it's difficult for players. Some of them get affected by it, get annoyed by it.

"They achieved massive successes. But also, they can help the club more, help the players more. There should be two ways that they support it. But I think always the thing you most love, you most criticise."

Perhaps that is why Ten Hag was so robust with his United players, even those he signed. Antony was the €100million (£84m, $112m) winger viewed as the biggest stick with which to beat Ten Hag. A player who he coached at Ajax arrived for one of the largest sums United have paid for a player, but delivered very little and had off-field issues. Ten Hag rates Antony as a player, but he twice tore into him after games over his positioning .

Antony's cost affected perceptions. In his first summer, Ten Hag found himself needing a right-winger late in the window due to Jadon Sancho's unexpected stance. "There came up a problem because Sancho didn't want to play on the right side; he said that," says Ten Hag. "Which was very weird; he played often on the right. He said he felt more comfortable on the left. So there we had an issue, and we were late."

Antony, also recommended by the scouting department, was bought as the right-winger on deadline day, with Ajax taking advantage of United's circumstances to extract a fee well above market rate.

Ten Hag denies a player's background influenced his selections. "I see on performances and profiles what is needed for the game," he says. "Not on emotion, if I like a player or dislike a player, or if I trained him before, or if I bought him or the club bought him, no, I can be acting very professional, I would say."

His manner has been called brusque, but away from the intensity of that job, he is personable and thoughtful. He is warm with John and Anita, who serve us a steak dinner.

Ten Hag's spell at Bayer Leverkusen was cold, even for the crazy world of football. He was sacked after three games in charge, having taken over from Xabi Alonso, who won the Bundesliga then went to Real Madrid.

"It's a very strange story," he says. "They ended an era with Alonso, so all the players wanted to go. We fought for some and they were not committed anymore. So it was waiting until September 1. The good players signed in the last couple of days. I never worked with them. Three games and then we parted ways."

Talk of Leverkusen leads Ten Hag to bring up Garnacho. "I regret where he is now," he says. "I told him, 'Come to Leverkusen'. But luckily he didn't. He wanted to stay in England. I understand, the best league, so he denied."

Ten Hag helped develop Garnacho into a Premier League player. His move to Chelsea hasn't worked out and now he is on loan at Aston Villa.

"He's a character, you have to manage him, but I had a strong connection with him," says Ten Hag. "But it's also up to him, of course, but he needs a coach, a particular coach, who will give him trust, who will give him love. He needs the love, definitely. But he's an amazing player. What's so special about him is he can run all day, high volume at really high speed, all game, back and forward.

"Sometimes his head is not on defending. So mentally, his mindset, you have to make sure he is focused and disciplined and does the job every transition, but he's capable of doing it and attacking-wise he can go forward and do incredible things, making dribbles, finishing. He can do the final pass, but sometimes he's a little bit selfish."

Ten Hag laughs. "But yeah, you balance this."

Ten Hag pulls out his laptop to show FC Twente's plans and data analysis. There is an image that depicts the team as a boat going downstream, passing by landmarks they need to hit. He also has pages of detailed statistical analysis, which he uses for recruitment.

"Seven points where I judge the player," he explains. "Technical ability, for me, is most important. Second is game intelligence and cognition. Third, you need athleticism, then lifestyle. Determination. Resilience and robustness to play every third day. And then we want to be always offensive.

"For instance, when I came to United, we didn't have the scoring ability to be in the top four. I will not say football is mathematics, but a bit of logic is in it. For us at Twente, we need 70 goals if you want to be in fourth position. When you want to win the Premier League, you need 85, 90 goals.

"I use this every day, so it should not be a document in a drawer. That is winning culture, if we match what we described. We use a lot of data to see new signings match our style of play."

Ten Hag continues: "Data changed the whole world, and now it's coming, AI, and every organisation has to take this on board. I think United miss some aspects. The moment I came in, they were starting. For instance, data was already a long time on board at Ajax."

Dominic Jordan was hired as United's first head of data in 2022. He has left, replaced by Michael Sansoni, an appointment by Sir Jim Ratcliffe after his company, INEOS, became minority owners of the club in December 2023 .

"A manager should get, by the end, all the information," says Ten Hag. "You need others in a club to collect all the information and make everything ready to make final decisions. Top organisations innovate continually and they're actually driving the innovations.

"I offered my knowledge and abilities to INEOS to help them to construct, but they were of the opinion that they knew already everything. They were convinced of, say, the philosophy, the strategy, the work methods. But they came from petrochemicals, from Formula 1, from cycling. Top football demands something totally different."

The next night, Ten Hag is in his element at FC Twente's Conference League tie against FC Thun, the Swiss champions. Ruud Nijstad - an 18-year-old left-sided centre-half already attracting interest from Europe's big clubs, including United - helps Twente keep a clean sheet on the way to a deserved 1-0 victory.

The atmosphere at the 30,000-capacity stadium is loud, and Ten Hag goes pitchside to conduct a television interview alongside former Ajax, FC Twente and Netherlands midfielder Ronald de Boer and Youri Mulder, technical director of Schalke 04. He believes it is useful for the appropriate executives to speak at the right times, so fans do not solely hear from the head coach.

"I agree you need more than one voice," he says later. "Selections and game plan, definitely the manager, the head coach. Culture, then it's probably more the technical director. Financial issues, then the CEO has to step forward."

Portraits of hundreds of Twente players line the corridors by the dressing room. Ten Hag points out one who is fondly remembered at both Twente and United. "He made the assist for Marco van Basten in the 1988 Euro final," he says, pointing to Arnold Muhren, who won the 1983 FA Cup with United. Ten Hag's own image is also on the wall.

Afterwards, he drives me to my hotel, and we discuss his work as a UEFA technical analyst. He is covering Paris Saint-Germain versus Barcelona from home because Twente travel to Gibraltar for their next Conference League game at Lincoln Red Imps, two days later.

Now 56, his love of football is undimmed.
